Question: What's your take on the Indian men's team winning its second consecutive bronze medal at the Paris Olympics 2024? What does the future hold for Indian hockey?

As a child in the 1990s and early 2000s, we became used to seeing India losing badly in hockey. There were only a few bright spots - 5th finish in the 1994 World Cup, 1998 Asian Games win, almost getting a place in the Sydney Olympic semifinal (when Poland denied India that chance by scoring an equalizer in the 70th minute), famous victories over Pakistan (1996 SAF games, 2003 Champions trophies), etc. India even failed to qualify for the 2008 Olympics. But the Indian hockey team has been on the rise in the last decade. Yes, they have not been very consistent at a high level but the team has been among the top 5–6 teams over the last 6–7 years. I was expecting India to finish 3rd in the pool but India’s first victory over Australia in the Olympics in 5 decades was the biggest highlight. Generations of Indians were accustomed to see India losing to Australia in the Commonwealth and Olympic games. Eventually, India finished second after losing to Belgium in the group stage and got a better draw to face Great Britain. The semi-final against Germany was a bad game. But even on that bad day the Indian team fought well and the last shot of the match was a brilliant save from the German goalkeeper. The overreliance on captain Harmanpreet Singh for converting penalty corner and the absence of Amit Rohidas cost us a place in the semifinal. The Bronze medal match was a good game and India came back from behind to beat Spain. PR Sreejesh was brilliant in the whole tournament along with the captain. A second consecutive bronze may not be considered a very good result for the Indian hockey team. The Indian team should have played in the final. Bronze may be a consolidation for the India team but the expectations were for a gold. Lets be very clear this team is strong and not the weak team of 1990s and 200s. The team played brilliantly but the inability to handle the pressure in the last few minutes of the semi-final was a let down. I am disappointed with a bronze in Paris but I hope the color of the medal will change in LA in 2028. Question: How are civil service aspirants fooling the UPSC system?

It is happening everywhere (entrance exams and government jobs) - Engineering/Medical/MBA entrance examination, admission to Government colleges, and all Government jobs (from low-level state jobs to UPSC civil service). And most of the UPSC aspirants are not doing all illegal things. They are just taking advantage of the loopholes. I was listening to Vikas Divyakirti. He gave some examples - 1) In the EWS category the whole family income of the last year (ITR) is considered. Sometimes, the family sells their land (permanently or temporarily) to fall in EWS criteria. Sometimes, one of the parents takes a long medical leave, and the aspirant takes a long leave (if he/she is working) so that their ITR income comes under the limit. 2) In the OBC non-creamy layer, the income of parents is only considered. And the children of Group A service can’t take advantage of OBC reservation. Sometimes, parents take VRS from their jobs and transfer their property to the aspirant. Now the parent’s ITR income falls under 8 Lakh. And agricultural income is not considered in the 8 lakhs. So, many rich people become “farmers”. In India, we all know that many people underreport their income in ITR forms. So, you will find many “rich” people (mainly from the business community and those having black money). So underreporting of income is very common in India. So, those having EWS and a non-creamy layer OBC certificate are valid certificates. And we all know that we can literally “buy” medical certificates. It may not be difficult to get a PH certificate. UPSC is the highest civil service exam in India and many aspirants do take advantage of the loopholes of the system.

Question: How do you see the results of the 2024 Lok Sabha election in Bihar?
Answer: The election results of the 2024 Lok Sabha election in Bihar have been on expected lines but the NDA lost many seats in the last phase of the election. NDA won 30 seats (12 BJP, 12 JDU, 5 LJP(R), and 1 HAM), INDI Alliance won 9 seats (RJD 4, Congress 3, and CPI(ML) 2), and Pappu Yadav is the lone independent MP. The vote share of NDA was around 47% and that of the INDI Alliance was around 39–40%. The vote share of the main parties were as - RJD 22.14 % (contested 23 seats), BJP 20.52% (contested 17 seats), JD(U) 18.52% (contested 16 seats), Congress 9.20% (contested 9 seats), LJP(R) 6.47% (contested 5 sears), CPI(ML) 2.99% (contested 3 seats). The best strike rate was of LJP(R) which won all 5 seats. NDA could have easily won 32–34 seats in Bihar. But one person - Bhojpuri cinema Superstar Pawan Singh brought down the tally of NDA by 3–4 seats. Pawan Singh was initially given the BJP ticket of Asansol in West Bengal but due to his past (where he had sung so many vulgar songs on Bengalis), his candidature was withdrawn. He wanted Arrah but BJP didn’t give him a ticket from Bihar. So Pawan Singh stood as an independent candidate from Karakat. Pawan Singh comes from the Rajput community and he was fighting Kushwaha’s community big leader and NDA candidate Upendra Kushwaha. Lalu Yadav also played the Kushwaha card well in Bihar and gave the community many seats. There was a perception in the Kushwaha community in the whole of Bihar (mainly in the Sahabad region) that the BJP wanted to defeat Upendra Kushwaha and thus they turned against BJP (mainly BJP’s Rajput MPs). BJP and NDA lost every seat of the Sahabad region - Sasaram, Karakat, Aurangabad, Arrah, Buxar, Jehanadab and even Patliputra. NDA lost 7 seats in South Western Bihar (south of Ganga river) and all of BJP’s defeats in Bihar (all 5) came from this region. NDA lost 3 seats in minority-dominated Semmanchal (Katihar, Purnea and Kishanganj). The last phase was not good for NDA (mainly BJP where it lost 4 seats). Apart from Pawan Singh factor two factors played a role in the last phase - 1) the Chhapra clash between Rajputs and Ydavs played a part in this phase. The Yadav community didn’t support BJP’s Ramkripal Yadav like earlier in Patliputra against Lalu’s elder daughter Misa Bharti and finally Misa Bharti was able to defeat Ramkripal Yadav in 3rd attempt. 2) a Bhumihar student leader of Patna University was killed in broad daylight and students from Yadav and Kurmi communities were accused of this murder BJP lost some of the votes of these communities in the 7th phase. As expected NDA lost the vote share and their victory margin decreased in almost every seat compared to 2019. RJD played the Kushwaha card well but it didn’t convert into seats. RJD tried to convert the contest in seats where NDA’s upper cast candidates were pitted against INDI Alliance OBC candidates as the fight between upper casts and lower casts. RJD also tried to get upper caste votes in some seats with upper caste candidates in Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Maharjganj etc. but they failed to win these seats. We did see some of the traditional caste battles in some seats - Rajput v/s Yadav (Saran) and Bhumihas v/s Rahput (Maharajganj and Vaishali). We saw fewer same caste fight this time - Banka and Madhepura (Yadav v/s Yadav), Bhagalpur (Gangota v/s Gangota), Muzaffarpur (Nishad v/s Nishad). On the pan Bihar level, these casts support NDA - General/Upper casts, Kumris, MBCs, a section of Dalits & a section of Kushwaha. These groups supported the INDI Alliance - Muslims, Yadavs, a small section of MBCs (like Nishad), a section of Dalits, a section of Kushwahas, & MBCs, a small section of upper caste etc. Many communities voted tactically and broke the traditional caste alliances. Like most parts of rural or semi-urban areas, Development didn’t play an important part in the Bihar election. The MP who worked most for his constituency - Former Union Minister R K Singh lost due to caste combinations in Arrah. RJD’s caste equation worked but not too much to convert this into seats. RJD played a dangerous game to ignite a caste war in Bihar. They succeded in Saran where one person was killed in a Yadav-Rajput clash. This was the first poll-related violence murder in many years. This violence helped RJD and Misa Bharti became the first member of Lalu family to win a Lok Sabha election after 2009. Lalu’s second daughter - Rohini Acharya lost the election. Some of the interesting seats in Bihar were as - Both alliances made many blunder. BJP’s weak candidate in Buxar helped RJD and BJP’s candidate over confidence in Sasaram resulted in a shock defeat for BJP. Had Nitish given ticket to a Bhumihar in Jehanabad, he would have won the seat. Nitish should have changed the candidate in Katihar against Congress Tariq Anwar. RJD made a mess in Purnia and Siwan. They gave 3 seats to VIP and VIP had to import candidates from RJD and BJP & all three lost. RJD failed to find a strong Yadav candidate in Madhepura (the Yadav bastion of Bihar). RJD lost Nawada due to infighting. Many NDA candidates faced anti-incumbency and was bailed only by Modi factor and Nitish MBC votes. The NOTA in Bihar was 2.4% and we can assume most of them were NDA voters. The 2024 Lok Sabha election has set the stage for the 2025 Bihar assembly election. Both alliances are strong and we will witness a mouthwatering contest in the assembly election.

Name: Achal
Question: Which is the most interesting name in the Modi 3.0 cabinet?
Answer: The most interesting name in the Modi 3.0 Cabinet is former Bihar CM Jitan Ram Manjhi. He is the Cabinet minister for micro, small, and medium enterprises. Jitan Ram Manjhi comes from the Musahar community. This community is one of the poorest Dalit communities in India. They are perhaps the most backward Dalit community. Musahar caste got its name on account of their traditional occupation as rat catchers/eaters. There are stories that these people used to eat rats in tough times. Musahar community lives in Bihar, Terai of Nepal, Eastern UP, and parts of Jharkhand. They constitute roughly 3% of the population of Bihar. Jitan Ram Manjhi is the first central minister from the community. Yes, he was an accidental CM of Bihar for 10 months but he was not given much freedom in that tenure. Sometimes, symbolism is very important in society. Jitan Ram Manjhi becoming a Union Cabinet minister gives hope to millions of people from the Musahar community is that there is hope for them also. This may uplift the spirit of the community and be a great example of social justice. Jitan Ram Manjhi is 79 years old and the oldest minister in Modi Cabinet, He is a known party hopper - starting from Congress to Janta Dal to RJD to JD(U) to his own party HAM. He is known for giving many mindless statements. But he is a political fighter. This was his third consecutive Lok Sabha election. He has lost the last two but this time he bounced back and won a tough election from the Gaya Lok Sabha seat. He is the lone MP from his party but still got a cabinet minister post. Narendra Modi has demonstrated that he is very serious about the real social justice and representation. This type of social justice is not like the social justice of Tejaswi Yadav or Akhilesh Yadav whose social justice is about their own family. Today, every member of the 50–60 lakh plus Musahar community would be feeling proud that one of them is a cabinet minister in Delhi. Modi has not taken away the reservation of SCs but given a Cabinet place to the most backward Dalit community leader.

Name: Achal
Question: Rahul Gandhi has accused BJP of the biggest stock market scam where PM Modi and HM Amit Shah asked people to invest after the result of exit polls. Is it a scam?
Answer: An exit poll is a statistic based on sampling. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, most Exit polls predicted all states correctly except three states. More than 64 voters voted in the election and it’s practically impossible to predict the Indian election. There is always a sampling error and Most Backward communities & women are often less represented in such polls. So, sometimes exit polls go wrong. In 2014 and 2019 most of the exit polls gave fewer seats to BJP and this time they gave more seats to BJP. The stock market jumped after the exit poll and nose-dived on 4th June when the BJP lost the majority. But as the NDA allies backed Modi the stock market was back to its level. Rahul Gandhi is wrong in saying that the Exit poll was a scam to earn money in the stock market. Now let me ask a question - Why does the stock market fear Congress? The answer is that Rahul Gandhi has become a hardcore leftist and his ideas and promises are wealth destroyers. Socialism in a nutshell means the distribution of poverty and destruction of wealth. Modi would have wished to control the share market. It has its own dynamics and it reacts to the political situation. Rahul Gandhi sees everything as a scam. By the way, if Congress had repeated its part two performances then Rahul Gandhi would have called EVMs and the election process also a scam.

Name: Achal
Question: After building Ram temple, airport and new railway station and roads, why is the Ayodhya seat lost?
Answer: Ram Mandir in Ajodhya is a civilizational issue for India and Sanatan Dharma. I don’t care who wins the Ayodhya assembly or Lok Sabha seat. Narendra Modi will always be remembered as the person who played a crucial role in building the Ram Mandir. This was the dream of so many generations of Hindus and the dream was fulfilled after 500 years. Obviously, a new airport was built and the railway station got a new makeover. Elections will come and go. Out of 17 times, the BJP has just won the Faizabad Lok Sabha seat 5 times. After 1992, they have won the seat 4 times and has lost the seat 4 times. This seat has always been tough for BJP due to various other reasons - the unpopularity of Lallu Singh, a fake narrative that the BJP would take out reservations by changing the constitution, SP’s brilliant ticket distribution, INDI Alliance promise that every woman of the poor family will get one lakh rupee annually, etc. Even despite all these things BJP did get more votes in Ayodhya assembly segment but Faizabad Lok Sabha seats have 4 other assembly segments also. Even in the 2019 election when BJP won most of the Hindi heartland seats by a big margin of many lakhs, the victory margin in Faizabad was just 65K. Ayodhya Ram Mandir is for billions of Hindus. I will have no complaints with the Ayodhya due to their voting preferences. In India, you don’t always win elections based on development work and there are many other important factors. BJP was not smart enough like SP and SP was better in handling the election campaign. The Ram Mandir is way beyond any election. Jai Shree Ram !!!

Name: Achal
Question: Why is Congress happy despite the loss?
Answer: As per a journalist who is very close to the Congress party, Rahul Gandhi’s life mission is to remove Narendra Modi. This time Congress along with its allies did manage to stop Modi from having a majority on his own. There may be “n” number of reasons for this but at the end BJP has “just” 240 MPs. This is the reason for the happiness of the Congress party. It’s another thing that BJP’s 2024 tally is more than Congress’s tally of 1991 (when Congress ran a minority Government for a full 5 years). BJP’s 2024 tally is their 3rd best tally and Congress’s tally of 99 is their third worst tally. Congress seems to be behaving like a winner with 99 seats. Winning and losing is about perception. The main aim of the Congress party in the 2024 election was to stop the BJP from getting the majority of its own as they knew that they would not be able to form the Government. Congress achieved this goal and they are celebrating their victory. From here onwards, Congress will try to remove Narendra Modi from the post of PM of India. Rahul Gandhi will channel all of his energy to discredit Modi 3 Government. But as of now its time for Congress to enjoy their 99 seats and let them enjoy before Modi 3.0 would hit them.

Name: Achal
Question: Is it right to say that the BJP lost its earlier majority because of Modi, or the BJP managed to win at least 240 seats only because of Modiji? Which one is more true?
Answer: BJP’s tally reached 240 seats due to Narendra Modi and BJP won just 240 seats due to Narendra Modi. Narendra Modi failed to counter the “fake” narrative of the INDI Alliance that the BJP would change the constitution and take away SC/ST/OBC reservations. BJP’s candidate selection was also not up to mark and Modi had a role in finalizing the names of those candidates. But at the same time, Narendra Modi helped many BJP candidates. His tireless campaign propelled many NDA candidates to victory. Many of these candidates were fighting a very tough battle. Let me give an example of my home state of Bihar - Saran Lok Sabha seat. BJP’s Rajiv Pratap Rudy was facing a very tough challenge from Lalu’s second daughter Rohini Acharya (who donated her kidney to Lalu Yadav). Modi’s rally lifted the chances of the BJP and Rudy won the seat despite all odds. But at the same time, the BJP lost many seats where Modi had campaigned. Some of the key decisions of Modi saved BJP and expanded NDA. Modi decided to bring Nitish Kumar in NDA on Jan 24 and it proved very critical. Without Nitish, the NDA tally in Bihar would have not even touched 15. BJP-JD(S) alliance worked very well in the Bengaluru-Mysuru region and this time BJP was able to defeat D K Shiv Kumar’s brother in his stronghold of Bengaluru Rural seat. BJP alliance with RLD and Shiv Sena worked to some extent. BJP would not have touched 240 seats without these strategic alliances. You can’t all the election to hit six on every ball. You will get some good delivery and you will struggle. But the key is to survive the difficult ball so that you can hit loose balls. Modi has politically survived and is still the most powerful Indian politician. He still has the strength and support of 36.56% Indians (43% for NDA). So, 43% of Indians voted to make Narendra Modi the PM for 3rd time. This number is more than any non-BJP alliance in the last 35 years.

Name: Achal
Question: Since the INDI alliance couldn't establish their government, will the alliance exist or will they break the alliance and work independently?
Answer: INDI Alliance may remain for some time in Delhi and in the parliament. But in states, there would be lot of infighting among INDI Alliance partners. The main aim of the INDI Alliance was to challenge Modi in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. The INDI Alliance failed to defeat Modi but they won a consolation prize by stopping BJP to 240 seats. The mood in the opposition alliance is good. Akhilesh Yadav has emerged as the most important INDI Alliance leader who on his own stopped BJP from touching the 272 seats. Other leaders like Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee, Stalin, Uddhav , Sharad Pawar also did good in their own turf. But sooner or later, they would realize that Modi is still here and NDA is ruling India. Before the next election, each of the parties will have to face the BJP & their allies in their home states in the assembly elections. Now the assembly election cycle will start for the next 5 years. In 2024, Congress may have a chance in Haryana, and elections in Maharashtra & Jharkhand would be very close. In 2025, the election is scheduled in Bihar and Delhi, and in 2026 many big states like West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, etc. will go to polls. Then the turn of UP, Gujarat will come. In many states, the INDI Alliance will fight with each other like West Bengal and Kerala. We don’t know whether Congress will give some seats to AAP in Haryana in the upcoming assembly election or not. There will be troubles in seat sharing in Maharashtra too as the resurgent Congress will demand a good share of seats. Meanwhile, some INDI Alliance partners may flirt with the BJP to get some benefits. For regional leaders, state assemblies are much more than national elections. If Akhilesh Yadav loses the next UP election then all his hard work will go to waste. The same is true for Left and at any cost they would like to maintain power in Kerala. The INDI Alliance may remain in Delhi but it will be difficult to maintain the alliance in states. It would interesting to see whether the alliance will be there in 2029 or not. Edit - AAP has already broken its alliance with Congress in Delhi.

Name: Achal
Question: Why is the AAP celebrating the results of the 2024 Lok Sabha election?
Answer: In India, people usually take pleasure in someone’s fall and forget their own condition. The condition of AAP is the same after the 2024 Lok Sabha election. The party is one of the biggest losers of the Lok Sabha election. AAP is ruling two states - Delhi and Punjab. Both states have 20 seats and AAP was contesting 17 seats and won just 3 seats. AAP’s vote share in Punjab was 26%. Just 2 years back AAP had won 92 seats out of 117 seats in the assembly election. Its not that AAP lost to BJP in Punjab but mainly lost to its national ally Congress. Lok Sabha election result in 2024 The main worry factor was that AAP was ahead in just 32 Assembly elections. Congress took the lead in 38 assembly segments and even the BJP was ahead in 23 assembly segments (Akali Dal was ahead in 15 seats). Punjab is witnessing a four-corner contest and AAP has lost the most ground compared to the last assembly election. It’s a big setback to AAP. Even in 2014, AAP had won 4 seats in Punjab. Let’s talk about Delhi. AAP maintained its tally of 2014 and 2019 in Delhi i.e. 0. This time AAP and Congress were in alliance. They did challenge the BJP and BJP’s vote share came down marginally to 54.34% votes from 56.86%. But it was enough for the BJP to defeat the INDI Alliance in Delhi. The lowest margin in Delhi was 78 K and the highest margin was 2.9 Lakh. Kejriwal came out of jail to campaign for AAP and he made the election about himself. But still, AAP lost all 4 seats. The 2024 Lok Sabha election is a big setback for AAP’s expansion. The party also contested one - one seat in alliance with Congress in Haryana and Gujarat. The party lost both seats. Now AAP is part of the INDI Alliance and can’t expand outside Delhi and Punjab. Congress at best can give a few seats in the upcoming Haryana Assembly election. The AAP’s top leadership is in jail and even though all of them come out of jail, the corruption allegation has dented the image of AAP forever. Now AAP is like a normal party. But still, AAP was celebrating the election result of the 2024 election. AAP is happy that their INDI Alliance stopped BJP to 240 seats even though the whole INDI Alliance could not match BJP’s tally. The role of AAP in stopping BJP was minimal. But AAP is taking happiness in BJP’s setback rather than introspecting themselves. Now, there is a good possibility that AAP may lose one or two states in the coming assembly elections. Even if they retain Delhi anyhow they will find it very difficult to retain Punjab. Now even INDI Alliance will not give more importance to AAP because they are a very small party with 1.1% votes and 3 Lok Sabha seats.

Name: Achal
Question: Is there any chance of I.N.D.I.A. to form a government in 2024?
Answer: Yes there is a chance that INDI Alliance can form Government in 2024. They can form the Government on social media. NDA has the majority in the Lok Sabha and it’s a pre-poll alliance. So it will get the invitation to form Government from President tomorrow. By the way BJP’s number is more than all of INDI Alliance. There are some wishful thinking that NDA allies will leave the NDA fold. It’s Modi 3.0 and INDI Alliance will have to wait at least 5 years (if not more) to form the Government. Even if one or two allies leave NDA, NDA can manage the majority. Remember that Congress successfully ran the Government between 1991 to 1996 with 244 seats. And if INDI Alliance will try to poach NDA allies then NDA can also do the same.

Name: Achal
Question: What could be the "sole" reason for the NDA not reaching the 400 target?
Answer: The sole reason for NDA not crossing 300 and BJP not getting the majority in its own is that the Caste factor played an important role in Hindu heartland. INDI Alliance’s main weapon to stop Modi was to divide Hindus on basis of caste. BJP wanted to unite Hindus and INDI Alliance wanted to break Hindus on basis of caste. In the battleground states of UP, Rajasthan and even in Bihar caste factor worked. There is nothing wrong into it as this is the reality of Indian politics. In 2019 and 2014 majority of Hindus has voted as political Hindu but this time a big section voted on basis of their caste. Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA vote bank worked. In UP Dalit vote bank of BSP favored SP over BJP and some non-Yadav OBC like Kurmi/Maurya community favored SP in Eastern UP. General caste also voted for INDI Alliance on seats where there were candidates from their own community. In Rajasthan, Haryana the election was in caste line. In Bihar, NDA lost 9 seats due to caste combinations. INDI Alliance narrative that BJP would change constitution with 400 seats and take away the reservation worked in parts of Hindi heartland. A big section of Dalits and OBC bought this issue and voted against BJP. INDI Alliance has been successful in dividing Hindus on basis of caste in Hindu heartland.

Name: Achal
Question: Who is the winner of the 2024 election?
Answer: NDA is the winner of the 2024 Lok Sabha election. But the real game changer of the election is Akhilesh Yadav. He led the INDI Alliance in UP and his alliance won 43 seats from UP with 43% votes. BJP could not reach the magic figure of 272 because of Akhilesh Yadav. Had BJP repeated the performance of 2019 and 2014 in UP, they would have easily got majority. In 2004 also, it was SP which defeated BJP in UP and helped Congress to end up willing more seats than BJP. And 20 years down the line, SP has defeated BJP and stopped BJP getting majority on his own. It’s the first election victory of Akhilesh Yadav and we must give him full credit.

Name: Achal
Question: How accurate do you think exit polls are in predicting the outcome of an election?
Answer: Most of the times exit polls are directionally correct. There have been some times like 2004 Lok Sabha election and 2008 Karnataka assembly election. By the way exit poll is a complex statistics and they follow their own methodologies. If the election is very tight or tide is turning from one direction to another direction then that’s also picked up by exit polls like 2023 Chhattisgarh assembly election. Many times some exit polls would pick party A as winner and others will pick up side B as winner. We have seen that one exit poll is predicting NDA’s victory in 2024 Andhra assembly election while other is predicting YSRCP’s win. The same case is true with exit polls of Odisha assembly election. If you look at the broader range of exit polls of the 2024 Lok Sabha election, all are predicting that NDA will secure majority. The lower margin is 280 seats and higher margin in 400 plus seats. Dainik Bhashkar has put the lower number of NDA to 281 and all others have put this number above 340. The direction is quite clear that NDA is coming to power. But exit polls vary a lot with exact number. It’s very difficult to predict the exact number of seats as some votes here and there can alter results of many seats. Tomorrow (4th June), we will see whether exit polls are directionally correct or not. If NDA fail to cross the majority mark, then Indian exit poll agencies will have to revisit their methodology and findings. But it’s very rare that all exit polls would miss a wave for INDI Alliance (as claimed by the alliance that they would win 295 seats). I am confident that NDA will get majority on its own tomorrow.

Name: Achal
Question: Exit poll is out & Congress is almost vanished. Who will take responsibility, Raul Gandi or Khadge?
Answer: No, Congress has not vanished and many exit polls are suggesting a better number for Congress (compared to 2014 and 2019). Congress won 44 seats in 2014 and 52 seats in 2019 and some exit polls have suggested that Congress could cross the 60 mark. If Congress manages to increase its tally it would be a “moral victory” for the Congress party. Many Congress-friendly analysts like Ravish Kumar have already started to praise Congress for its fight in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. This time Congress seems to have increased its head-to-head percentage compared to 2019 against BJP. As per exit polls, Congress can open its account in Rajasthan & Haryana and can wrest a couple of seats in Jharkhand (all against BJP). Congress may be able to do relatively well in Punjab against its national ally AAP. The silver lining for Congress is that they have been able to attract minority votes in many states. The exit poll also shows that Congress is not able to stop BJP in most of the states. Congress recently won Telangana and Karnataka but as per exit poll, BJP will defeat them in both states. Congress is marginally able to improve its tally in a couple of states but they may be routed in many direct fight seats. The single biggest problem for Congress is that its tallest leader Rahul Gandhi is a freeloader without any responsibility. If Congress loses the 2024 Lok Sabha election then it would be a loss of face for Mallikarjun Kharge. Rahul Gandhi is just an MP and he hold no position in the party. So, Rahul Gandhi can’t be blamed for any bad thing. However, he will get credit for all the good performances of the party. This is the party that was without a full-time president for three and half years after 2019. How can you expect them to mount a challenge when their biggest leader is just a freeloader without any responsibility? Rahul Gandhi will remain the tallest leader of the party for coming decades irrespective of any election result because his party is a family enterprise. If exit call holds then Congress party needs to introspect but they will not do that and blame the EVMs and Modi.

Name: Achal
Question: Will the NDA be able to reach 400 in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections?
Answer: This is the poll of major exit polls of the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Only one poll (Chanakya - which had predicted 2014 and 2019 well) has given NDA the magic number of 400. However, the upper limit for India Today-Axis is 401 but their average is 381. As of now, it seems difficult that NDA would cross the 400 mark. A 400 mark would mean that NDA has to sweep North, East, and West completely and make good inroads in South. NDA seems to be losing some seats in UP, Maharashtra, Bihar, and Rajasthan. If NDA sweeps these states like UP - 70 plus seats, Bihar - 35 plus, Maharashtra - 35 plus, and Rajasthan - all seats they they will have some chance. Also, they will have to sweep Odisha, win 25-plus seats in West Bengal, win 10-plus seats in Telangana, make heavy inroads into Tamil Nadu & Kerala, sweep Centra India and Gujarat, etc. All these seem to be difficult for now. The biggest issue is that INDI Alliance has been able to turn the 2024 Lok Sabha election in some states into an election about caste. This is the reason NDA is not able to completely sweep Bihar, and Rajasthan. Maharashtra is way complex and INDI alliance is strong there. But we must remember that the winning alliance is able to get more seats in the final tally. Let’s be very clear, if NDA is able to cross 350 and BJP is able to cross 303 mark it would be an excellent result for PM Modi and BJP. He may become first PM to win three consecutive elections and increase the seat tally every time. By the way everything is assumptions and predictions. Let’s wait till 4th June to get the real numbers.

Name: Achal
Question: What has been the biggest takeaway from the 2024 Lok Sabha election exit polls?
Answer: The biggest takeaway for me from the 2024 Lok Sabha exit poll is that BJP may again emerge as the single largest political party from South India (in terms of the number of MPs). Congress supporters and some leftist liberals have been floating a theory that South India is different from North India in terms of politics. But if the exit poll numbers hold then we can say that South India is not very different from North India. As per exit polls, INDI Alliance may dominate two states - Tamil Nadu and Kerala. NDA may sweep two states - Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Telangana is tight and few exit polls are saying that the BJP will win more seats than Congress and a few are saying that Congress & BJP may win equal number of seats. If BJP wins Telangana then NDA will have a 3–2 lead in South India even though INDI Alliance will win more seats from South India. BJP may emerge as the only party to open account in all 5 Southern states. And even in the two states where INDI Alliance has an edge, NDA may increase its vote tally significantly. BJP may create history if it opens an account in both Tamil Nadu and Kerala. It is almost certain that the BJP’s vote share in these two states is increasing significantly. If these results hold true then the theory that BJP is the party of North and West would go for a toss. We may vote differently, we may speak different languages, and we may have some differences but in the end, we all are Indians. If North, West, and East are voting for Modi the obviously he will get some traction in South India. BJP has worked very hard in South India and even though they have a long road ahead they are on the right path. BJP was the number 1 party in 2019 from South India and they may retain that title in 2024 also. The fun part is that the anti-BJP people may start pointing fingers at Karnataka, Andhra, and Telangana for voting for NDA-

Name: Achal
Question: Congress manifesto, Nyay Patra, promises to provide legal guarantee of minimum support price (MSP) to farmers. Isn't this the minimum the country should do for our 'Annadata'?
Answer: If you are ready to buy Aata 150 KG and Rice Ra 200 KG, then the condition of farmers will improve. Who will foot the bill of MSP guarantee? Are you ready to pay more direct or indirect taxes? The answer is most probably No. The middle class in India is one of the biggest hurdle in farmer’s prosperity. The middle class start to cry when the proves of agricultural products like vegetables and crop go up. The salary of a person might have increased many folds in last few decades but the prices of agricultural products has not increased that much. I remember three BJP state Governments lost power on the issue of onion price in 1998. Congress manifesto is full of such promises which can’t be fulfilled without bankrupting finances of Central Government. Congress knows that there very less chance that they would come to power. So they have put such absurd promises in its manifesto. If Congress comes to power and implements all of its big promises then the middle class will be the biggest sufferers. Please stop this narrative of “Annasata”. A framer is as import as a worker or a scientist, or a shopkeeper or an office going person, or an any other Indian. Farmers are not special and they are as important as any other professional. This is another issue that Indian society and Government has let down farmers.

Name: Achal
Question: As Congress claims, will the 2024 election results be a repeat of 2004?
Answer: There are many differences between 2004 and 2024 - The most important thing is that like Congress, the current leadership of BJP is also aware of 2004 and they have learned many lessons from that defeat. After 1st round of low turnout, BJP’s leadership burnt the midnight oil to change its strategy to avoid a repeat of 2004. BJP has learned much more than the 2004 results from Congress. Irrespective of the result of the 2024 Lok Sabha election, one thing seems certain - the BJP would win at least 2.5 more seats than the Congress.

Name: Achal
Question: What is your prediction for the upcoming elections? Do you think the BJP will win a majority and come back to power?
Answer: The Indian General election is the hardest election to predict in the world. India has 970 million registered voters (which is almost 3 times the population of the third largest country by population - the USA). India is very diverse and the election issues are very different from one region to another region. Many times pollsters and experts have gone wrong about elections in India. The biggest example is the 2004 Lok Sabha election. Even in the 2019 election, very few pollsters predicted 350 plus seats for NDA. This is the snapshot of the opinion and exit poll of the 2019 election. Image Source - Wikipedia Very few of the polls were giving an absolute majority to BJP but the BJP surprised everyone and secured 303 seats. Yogendra Yadav had predicted that BJP would not cross the 200 mark in the 2019 election. It’s another thing that we call the 2019 election as a wave election. But the election was considered so tight that Rahul Gandhi had invited leaders like Stalin, Akhilesh Yadav, and Tejashwi Yadav to become ministers in the Centre (a day before the counting). Now let us come to the 2014 Lok Sabha election. As of now, we can say that there were (and are) no wave in favor or against any party in whole country. There are many issues - performance of Modi Government, Reservations, Constitution, reservations on religious lines, Ram temple, Labharti schemes, freebies, caste, etc. But despite all these issues, one issue was present everywhere - the Modi factor. Some people went out to vote for Modi and some people voted to defeat Modi. Opposition succeded in making the election on caste equation and BJP failed to unite all Hindu casts in many parts of the country. The election came down to organizational strength and booth management. Different phases had different issues. The main issue was the constitution and reservation. The opposition accused that Modi would change the constitution and take away reservation in for two phases. It seemed that BJP was going in the same trap as the 2015 Bihar assembly election. But Modi counter-attacked and said that Congress would take away OBC, SC/ST, and give reservations to minorities. This was the turning point as Congress could not counter it effectively due to its past records. And now in last phase, Rahul Gandhi is not talking about the constitution at all. There is a big section of silent voters who don’t talk with journalists or among each other openly - Women voters and Most backward castes (non-dominant OBC and non-dominant SCs). It seems that women have overwhelmingly supported NDA in North India and the “labahrati” class (who are mostly MBCs) have also voted for NDA in many states. The Ram temple is more important for women in North India than men (in general) and the safety & security in states like UP & Bihar has generated sympathy among women. 73-year-old Modi has worked much harder than 53-year-old Rahul Gandhi despite being in power. Modi gave 80 plus interviews and he was seen almost every day on some or other channel. If Rahul Gandhi would have worked so hard then it might have helped Congress. e.g.- Modi came to Bihar 7–8 times and Rahul Gandhi came to Bihar just twice. My prediction is that NDA is on course for a third straight victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. But at the same time, no election is a done deal till the results are out and there is a very very remote possibility that NDA may loose the election. Modi is most likely going to become the first PM after Nehru to win three straight general elections and also he may become the first PM to increase his tally in all three elections. Let’s revisit all our assumptions after June 4th, 2024.

Name: Achal
Question: Can an injunction be obtained from the SC to prevent the telecast of Modi's visit to Kanniyakumari till the last phase of polling is over on June 1?
Answer: Narendra Modi is also a citizen of India and he has all the rights as a citizen of India. Narendra Modi has decided to mediate in Vivekanand rock in Kanyakumari after the end of campaign of the last phase of the election. Obviously media would follow Modi because Modi is the most popular politician of India. No one (including SC) has any right to stop Modi from visiting Kanyakumari and asking news channels / social media platforms not to cover Modi’s visit. It’s none of their business. It’s not duty if SC and Election Commission to direct media what to show or not show. This visit is not going to disturb social harmony or can case threat to any Indian. It seems you are obsessed with Modi. Can’t Modi go and visit any part of India? Rahul Gandhi doesn’t allow media in his Thailand or Europe visit. If he allows then media will follow him there. It seems that you have concluded that you are fearful of Modi factor. Indian public (of last phase) has already decided about their vote. So please don’t worry (Just chill) and wait till 4th June.

Name: Achal
Question: Is Swati Maliwal case plotted by BJP?
Answer: Yes, it’s a plot by BJP. BJP sent a lady AAP MP (who has been with Kejariwal for close to two decades from his NGO days) to CM house to “falsely” accuse Kejriwal’s PA of assault. That lady AAP MP knew the power of AAP social media and she still risked the wrath of that section of social media. The lady MP is facing character assassination on the social media by AAP supporters. And then BJP fabricated the medical report of AIIMS Delhi. Question: Why is the ECI not disclosing data under Form 17C? Is a major fraud expected?

Under rule 49S(2), the presiding officer of the polling booth has to provide a copy of the data entered in Form 17C to the polling agents of the candidates at the time of the close of polling. The original form 17C is sealed with the EVM in the presence of the polling agents. As per the Election Commission of India, “It is submitted that there is no legal mandate to provide Form 17C to any person other than the candidate or his agent”. ECI has also said that “ Form 17C on its website could lead to ‘mischief’ and that there is a possibility of manipulation of images, fostering ‘widespread discomfort and mistrust’. The election commission has never disclosed Form 17C in public and it’s doing the same now. Question: Which government stopped the caste census in India?
Answer: The modern nationwide census in India was started by the British in 1891. They used to conduct the census every 10 years. British Government conducted census till 1931. Caste/groups of all religions (Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, etc.) were recorded in all those censuses. The British Government didn’t conduct the general census in 1941 due to the Second World War. At that time British Empire was on the verge of loss at hands of Germany & Japan and the British Indian Government decided to postpone the caste census. Britain won the second world war but by 1945 it was clear that Britain would not be able to hold its Indian colony for a long time. India gained independence in 1947 and was also partitioned. The new Indian Government also had various other priorities and thus census was not conducted in the 1940s. Independent India decided to conduct its first census in 1951. Nehru Government decided to stop asking the caste question in the census. The logic given was that India needed to move away from a divisive approach and promote national unity. After that, India continued to conduct the general census every 10 years. Till now all censuses in India have been conducted under the Congress government except the one in 2001 (which was conducted by the Vajpayee government). There was a national consensus among all political parties before the 2011 census that the caste column should be included in the census form. But at the last moment, the Congress Government decided to drop the idea of including the caste column from the census question lists. In place of this. Congress Government came up with a separate census- the 2011 Socio-Economic and Caste Census. The general census is conducted by teachers and its conducted in the month of Feb but the 2011 Socio-Economic and Caste Census was conducted by relatively less educated and less effective groups like Aanganwadi groups without any fixed timeline. Obvious there was a big mismatch of all the data (or there may be different reasons) and the report of the 2011 Socio-Economic and Caste Census was never officially published. I clearly remember that our family was not counted in that census as no one came to our home. The Congress Government was so serious about this caste census that the census was not complied with before the 2014 election & the final report was compiled in Nov 2014 but its data was considered unreliable and the full data were not published. The Modi Government postponed the 2021 census due to the Coronavirus pandemic. Now it’s quite interesting that Rahul Gandhi is talking about conducting the caste census in the 2024 Lok Sabha election even though it was Congress that discontinued the caste census in 1951 and deliberately stopped it in 2011 (at that time Rahul Gandhi was an MP and General Secretary of the Congress party). One can always change the thoughts and change is the only constant thing in life. Congress has 3 CMs but they have not started any caste census in any of those 3 states. The first Siddaramaiah government had conducted a caste survey in Karnataka (I also gave my data in that survey) but they never published it (even though now Siddaramaiah is back as CM for the second time). Let Rahul Gandhi acknowledge the mistakes of the past (including his own) and then promise the caste census and then the Indian public may believe him.

Question: Why did Congress wait till the last day of nomination to announce Rahul Gandhi’s name as Congress candidate from Raebareli?
Answer: Congress delayed the announcement of its candidates from Amethi and Raebareli till the last day of nomination to deny the BJP a chance to put up a strong candidate from Raebareli. We will have to go back in history to understand this strategy. It was the 1999 election and Sonia Gandhi had recently entered into politics. It was expected that Congress would field her from Amethi (the seat of her late husband Rajiv Gandhi). But Congress had lost the seat for the first time to BJP in 1998 and Congress was also in search of another safe seat from South India. But there was a risk that the BJP could also field a strong candidate from the second seat of Sonia Gandhi. So, Congress tried to create the confusion about the seat. They planted stories that Sonia Gandhi could contest from Cudappah (Andhra Pradesh), Bellary (Karnataka), and Medak (Andhra Pradesh). The buzz was that Sonia could contest from either Cudappah or Bellary. At that time, NDA was ruling Centre, Andhra (TDP), and Karnataka (JD(U). Sonia Gandhi went to Hyderabad from Delhi in a commercial flight. At Hyderabad, there was one small private jet and one helicopter waiting. The plane was scheduled to fly to Cudappah and helicopter to Bellary so the BJP couldn’t guess the seat of Sonia Gandhi. It was the last date of nomination. BJP & TDP had got a hint about Sonia’s strategy and they had persuaded actress Vijayashanti to fight against Sonia from Cudappah seat. But somehow at the last moment, the BJP got the hint that Congress was bluffing and somehow they were able to convince Sushma Swaraj to contest against Sonia Gandhi from Bellary. They were able to transport Sushma Swaraj to Bellary before 3 PM on the last day of the nomination via a helicopter from Bengaluru[1] . Sonia Gandhi also filed her nomination papers for the same seat on the last day. The 1999 Bellary election between Sonia Gandhi and Sushma Swaraj remains one of the classical & fierce political battles of Indian history. Sonia Gandhi won the election by 56K votes. Congress wanted the same strategy for the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It was expected that Congress would declare the candidates from Amethi and Raebareli after the election in Kerala (26th April). Congress delayed the announcement till 3rd May (the last date of nomination) but they created a buzz that Raul Gandhi could contest the election from either one seat out of Amethi and Raebareli. Congress sympathizers created a buzz that Rahul would contest from Amethi. At last, BJP decided its own candidate from Raebareli - Dinesh Pratap Singh on May 2nd. The news of Rahul’s candidature came on the morning of May 3rd. On the night of May 2nd, Congress created an impression that Rahul was going Amethi. The party offices and guest houses of both seats Amethi and Raebareli were cleaned and the preparation was going on on both seats for Rahul’s nomination. There was a buzz that the BJP could give very strong candidates from Raebareli against Rahul Gandhi and Congress wanted to avoid such a situation. So, Congress created all this buzz that Rahul Gandhi was contesting from Amethi. It seems that Congress have succeeded in its strategy and Rahul Gandhi is not facing a strong BJP leader in Raebareli. But Congress has lost the battle of perception and it is widely believed that Rahul Gandhi fled Amethi due to fear of losing at the hands of Smriti Irani.

Name: Achal
Question: AstraZeneca, a British pharmaceutical giant, has admitted that its Covid-19 vaccine can result in a rare side effect of TTS. Majority of Indians have got this Covishield vaccine and how will it affect Indians?
Answer: We all take Paracetamol. Do you know that an “unintentional” overdose of Paracetamols is the most common cause of acute liver failure in the UK and USA? So, should we stop taking Paracetamol? For the first time AstraZeneca (the company that made the Covishield Vaccine with Oxford University) has accepted that in very very rare cases, the Covishield vaccine can cause a type of blood clotting (a disease called TTS). There have been earlier reports in media that the Covishield can cause TTS but the company has accepted this for the first time. But Covishield is not the only Corona vaccine that has side effects. All other major Corona vaccines like Pfizer, Moderna, Jhonson & Jhonson have known side effects. Covishield is a traditional vaccine but the Pfizer and Moderna vaccine uses the new mRNA technology and many people across the world have accused these mRNA vaccines of many side effects (like fatal heart attacks, deadly heart problems etc). Around 80 to 90 percent of Indians have received Covishield vaccine. The Covishield vaccine was given the go-ahead by almost every country of the world. Covishield was also approved by WHO. India’s Serum Institute was the biggest manufacturer of the Covishield vaccine and India exported these vaccines to over 90 countries. Normally it takes 5 to 10 years to develop a vaccine but the Coronavirus Pandemic was such a big threat to humanity that scientists across the globe created many vaccines within a few months and all Governments gave them emergency usage certificates. Ideally, these vaccines should not have been approved so quickly but it was a race against time. Some people in the world may have died or may have got complicated diseases due to Corona vaccine (cases are going on in courts of Western countries) but these vaccines have saved millions of lives. As per AstraZeneca’s statement in British Court, the company said that their Covishield vaccine saved the lives of 65 million people worldwide. Goverments had to take decision and they chose a path which has saved much more lives. We all remember the horrors of the second wave of the Coronavirus Pandemic when India was brought to its knees by the virus but we were able to take subsequent waves due to Covishield vaccine. The other option for India was the Pfizer mRNA vaccine and later it turned out that this vaccine also had some side effects. Pfizer Vaccine was very costly (Covishield was not patented and its formula was given to India without profit by Oxford University) it needed deep freezers to keep it very cool. India could have afforded the cost of the Pfizer Vaccine but India could not have distributed these vaccines due to lack of deep freezers in remote villages. Almost all of us would have lost many of our family members and friends without Covishield. This has saved the lives of millions of Indians who would have died in 3rd and 4th wave of the pandemic. As per some studies, 2 to 3 lakh people in America have died due to coronavirus due to their refusal to take the vaccine. But at the same time, let’s accept the side effects also. There is not a single drug in the world that has no side effects. And many more Indians die due to “casual” use of antibiotics. If you want to keep your family safe please stop using eating antibiotic tablets in normal circumstances. And most of the side effects of Coronavirus vaccines are seen in the first few days/months of taking the vaccine doses. So, we all are safe and there is no need to panic. If you get blood clotting then consult doctor and take the prescribed medication. As per some reports the side effect has been seen in less than 40 people out of 1.75 cr plus people and the rate of side effect is 0.00000007%. I support the decision of the Modi Govt. and our institutions (like IMCR) to use Covishield in 2021. That was the best decision based on the circumstances. That was a war-like situation and the decision was 100% correct based on all the available information. And, I also the Serum Institute which produced so many vaccines very quickly. Do you know that some people die due to drinking “excess” milk? Do you know that wheat increases the chances of death in some diseases? Do you know that some people have died after eating rice? If you are eating any medicine (or even food) then please go and read the side effects of those on the internet. There are almost 8 billion people on the earth and everything is bad for someone.

Question: Is it legally possible for the Prime Minister of India to hold the position for life? What would be the consequences if this were to happen?
Answer: Yes, it is legally possible that one person can remain PM of India for his/her whole life. There is only one condition - He/She has to win an election after every 5 years. India’s first PM Pandit Nehru was PM for his whole life (democratically). He first became PM of the interim Government in 1946 and then became PM of the Dominion of India in 1947. In 1946, he was not elected Congress President (who would have become PM of India) and he had 0 votes. But he became PM of India after Mahatma Gandhi’s intervention when Sardar Patel (who had the highest votes) withdrew. Nehru was “unelected PM till 1952 and after that, he won 3 consecutive elections (1951–52, 1957, and 1962). He died in 1964 while he was PM of India. Nehru remained PM of India for his whole life. I would not go into debate whether he was good or bad. But was was literally PM of India for his whole life from the time he became PM.

Question: Why is the Gandhi dynasty losing its sheen and shine despite efforts to keep it alive and active?

Name: Achal
Question: Why does Congress want to implement inheritance tax in India during the 2024 election campaign?
Answer: Congress manifesto and Rahul Gandhi’s speeches contain many freebies promises and wealth distribution. India can’t afford these freebies and Congress plans to tax Indian people more. I would thank Sam Pitroda for being honest in saying that Congress is considering inheritance tax. The idea of caste-wise economic survey and wealth distribution is absurd and ultra-leftist. On, top of that Congress has promised many freebies and notable freebies are One lakh rupees per annum to one woman per family, one lakh rupee to each graduate, etc. The promise of “One lakh rupees per annum to one woman per family” would need roughly 16 lakh crore per annum. From where the money would come? So, Congress would raise taxes and seize the properties of rich people (in the name of wealth distribution). By the way, America doesn’t have a federal inheritance tax and six states have an inheritance tax. In many Western countries, there is some kind of inheritance tax. In the West people spend most of the money on themselves and leave the residual money for their children. But in India, people save the money for future generations sacrificing their pleasure and lifestyle. So, the concept of Inheritance tax doesn’t suit India. Congress Government had imposed an Inheritance tax in India in 1953 and it was abolished by Congress itself in 1985. The tax rate was 7.5%. In last few decades Congress have been talking about this inheritance tax. India of 2024 is richer than India of 1985 and if inheritance tax is imposed in India again then a good number of people will fall under this category. In the last few decades, the price of land has gone many folds and normal people holding even smaller land may have to pay this tax. And Sam was hinting the tax is around 55%. Even if Congress fixes the inheritance tax to 30% then it would mean that you will have to pay 30% tax on your assets after your death. This would devastate many Indian families. Even many poor Indian farmers have land worth crores (in cases a new highway or railway is built on their land). A small shop even in a semi-urban town can cost lakhs and crores. Indian economy may be devasted if Congress wins the 2024 Lok Sabha election as Congress has become an ultra-left party. The party is talking about taking people’s wealth in the name of wealth distribution and then they will tax whatever is left after your death. I hope Indian voters will see this and save India from communist ideas. We have an example in hand - West Bengal. West Bengal was a leading state before the communist takeover and we have seen the economic destruction of the state.

Name: Achal
Question: Will Congress win more than 100 seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections?
Answer: Congress is contesting 330 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha election and this is its lowest tally in Indian electoral history. The math is very simple and Congress needs to win 30% of the seats to cross the 100-seat mark. So Congress needs to win 3 seats out of the 10 seats it’s contesting. In some states, the strike rate needs to be around 50% as Congress would find it difficult to have a strike rate of even 20% in many states. It is expected that Congress will have a very good strike rate in some states like Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Congress is contesting 9 seats in Tamil Nadu and it may win up to 7 to 8 (or even 9 seats) in the state. Congress is contesting 16 seats in Kerala and may win 10 to 14 seats in the state. So, the Congress strike rate in these two states may be around 80%. On the flip side, Congress at best can win one to two seats in Gujarat. In MP and Rajasthan, Congress is not expected to win big. So, it leaves Congress dependent on Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Punjab. Congress is contesting 17 seats in Maharashtra, 27 in Karnataka, and 13 seats in Punjab. Unless Congress sweeps these three states, it will be difficult for them to cross 100 seats. At best Congress can win 10–16 seats at max (from Delhi, UP, West Bengal, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar). If they perform their best they can have 10 seats from North East. These are all best-case scenarios. It would be very difficult for Congress to have 100 seats but if they can sweep Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Punjab then their tally would be close to 100.

Name: Achal
Question: What changes has Congress promised in EWS (economically weaker section) reservation in its 2024 election manifesto?
Answer: Congress has promised an overhaul of the reservation system in India. We all know that Congress has promised to increase the caste-based reservation. But there is one interesting thing in the Congress manifesto - Congress would like to change the EWS reservation criteria. The EWS (Economically weaker section) reservation was implemented in 2019 by the Modi Government. EWS is the category of people having an annual family income of less than 8 lakh rupees and who do not belong to any category such as SC/ST/OBC/MBC. The EWS reservation was challenged in the Supreme Court and the Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Constitutional Amendment which implemented EWS reservation. Supreme Court said that SC/ST/OBC can be excluded from EWS reservation and EWS reservation doesn’t breach the 50% ceiling of reservation. Modi Government’s stand is clear - all other groups have the reservation and EWS is exclusively for the non-reserved category. Now Congress is saying that they would give caste-based reservations to everyone. This would mean that the general category’s space would shrink. Tamil Nadu has 69% reservation, Bihar has 65% reservation, Jharkhand has 77% reservation and Chhattisgarh has 58% reservation (all caste-based reservation). All these states have 10% EWS reservations. If SC/ST/OBC are included in EWS then it would hard general category. Rahul Gandhi (if voted to power) would increase the reservation up to 70% and then there would be 10% EWS. On top of this Congress will introduce women’s reservation. So, hardly anything would be left for the general category and the poor section from the general category would suffer a lot. As of today, SC/ST/OBC can compete in 90% quota (it varies as per individual category like OBC in 40% un-reserved plus 27% OBC) as they can also compete in non-reserved general seats. When they are included in EWS then they can compete in full quota. It seems that Congress has abandoned the general category altogether. The general category knows that reservations are going to increase. When the caste-based reservation was increased by 10% in Bihar there was no protest from the general category. But they don’t publicly like the party that blames everything on caste inequality. Yes, Caste inequality was (and is) bad and it must be eradicated and reservation is a way towards this. But we should also think about the poor and deprived section of the un-reserved category. Rahul Gandhi is blaming every problem in India on caste inequality and it may or may not attract OBC votes but it has the potential to alienate the general category away from Congress.

Question: How do you see the first phase of polling for the 2024 Lok Sabha election in Bihar?
Answer: Bihar has voted for 4 Lok Sabha seats in the first phase of the 2024 Lok Sabha election - Jamui, Gaya, Aurangabad, and Nawada. As per reports, it is still Advantage NDA but everything is not going well for NDA. The voter turnout has remained low and there may be the following reasons for low voter turnout in the first phase - As per reports NDA may win two seats (both reserved for SCs)- Gaya and Jamui and they may have sailed through in Aurangabad somehow. Jamui was not very easy for Chirag Paswan’s brother-in-law Arun Bharti but the “abuse video” may have saved NDA. A video in which an RJD supporter was seen abusing Chirag’s mother and sister at Tejashwi rally and this has helped NDA in Jamui. It seems that former Bihar CM Jitanram Manjhi may become lucky in Gaya in 3rd time. He has lost last two elections and it seems that he has the edge in Gaya over RJD’s Kumar Sarvjeet. BJP’s Sushil Kumar Singh has faced a very tough challenge from RJD’s Abhay Kushwaha (a former JD(U) leader who switched sides just before the election) in Aurangabad. But it seems BJP may have a slight edge and Congress's big leader Nikhil Kumar has not openly supported RJD. But Nawada seems wide open. It was a safe seat for BJP but Lalu’s strong coalition had dented BJP. RJD has given the ticket to Sharvan Kushwaha and he has the support of Ashok Mahato (the villain of web series - Khakee the Bihar chapter). As per reports Kushwaha (traditionally the supporter of Nitish) has moved towards RJD and in some sections of Nitish’s cast Kurmi has also sided with RJD. A similar trend has been seen in Aurangabad. But the biggest worry for the BJP is that its core supporters Bhumihas didn’t come out in large numbers in Nawada to support BJP’s Bhumihar candidate Vivek Thakur. The voting percentage in Bhumihar dominated assembly seat Barbigha (where JD(U)’s Bhumihar MLA Sudarshan Kumar didn’t support BJP) was very low. The only silver lining for BJP is that Vinod Yadav (brother of RJD strongman Rajballabh Yadav) has contested the election as an independent candidate. In case Vinod Yadav gets 50 K plus votes then the BJP can win otherwise it’s difficult for the BJP. The rallies of Modi, Amit Shah, and Yogi have helped the BJP in these 4 seats but it’s still not enough to repeat the 2019 result. The best-case scenario for NDA is 4–0 and the worst-case scenario for NDA is 2–2. Even if NDA loses even one seat it would be a blow for BJP. We have seen less voter turnout than last time all over India but as per reports, BJP’s machinery in UP has been able to bring out voters (even its core voters) to the booth but Bihar BJP has failed to do the same. The only consolation news for BJP in these 4 seats is that Muslims (who are not very happy with RJD for giving them fewer tickets) have also not come out to vote in mass numbers like in previous elections. The less voter turnout means the victory margin will be far less than the 2019 election. BJP needs course correction in Bihar and it needs to keep its (& Nitish) core vote intact and make sure the Kushwaha community doesn’t lean towards RJD. BJP’s state President and Deputy CM Samrat Chaudhary is a leader of Kushwaha and if BJP can give an indication that he may become CM candidate in the next assembly election then BJP can stop the Kushwaha community from going to RJD’s fold. The common voters of Bihar are not very enthusiastic about the election and in such an election the alliance having better organizational strength wins. Modi’s 2024 future hinges on Bihar and if BJP state organization strength has to fight the election with 200% force otherwise Modi’s election machinery may suffer a setback in Bihar. RJD-led alliance has also made many mistakes in Bihar and now the Bihar election is dependent on the organization’s strength and charisma of big leaders like Modi or Lalu Yadav.

Question: Why is Rahul talking about the caste census so much? Is it really that important?
Answer: Rahul Gandhi is like a child who plays with a new toy but forgets it after some time. The “Caste Census” is a new political toy for Rahul Gandhi. If Bihar can do a caste census then Telangana and Karnataka can also do the same. So, till now Congress doesn’t seem to be very serious about this issue. If Congress performs well in the 2024 Lok Sabha election then Rahul Gandhi will talk about the caste census for some time but if BJP wins the 2024 Lok Sabha election, Rahul Gandhi may forget about this issue also.

Question: In India, if everyone is against corruption, then who is corrupt?

Name: Achal
Question: What is your opinion on "India’s debt under the Modi government surges 50% to Rs. 82 lakh crore"?
Answer: There is no doubt that India’s external debt has increased significantly. But as a percentage of GDP India’s external debt has decreased. During UPA years the external debt to GDP ratio was around 24% which has now come down to just over 18%. If you take overall debt of Indian central Government, India is in much better condition that major developed economies. India’s debt is around 83% if GDP but that if Japan is 261% and that of USA is around 121%. The total debt of American Federal Government is around 34 trillion dollars and that of Indian Central Government is around 2.06 trillion dollars. Let’s be very clear that debt fuels the economies of the world. But these debts must be used in productive work like capital expenditure. India needs investments of billions of dollars every year and obviously we don’t have that amount of money and we would take loan for these projects. Till the time loans are being used for capital expenditure we should not be too much worried about this. We must not forget the Coronavirus years which increased the debt of every economy of the world due to much more pending and less revenue. I would say Indian debt is under control and there is no need to worry about it till the time we growing economically at good pace.

Name: Achal
Question: Do you trust the BJP's "Modi ki guarantee"?

Question: What are your comments on Modi making 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047?
Answer: That’s the dream and vision of Modi. Former President Abdul Kalam used to say that we need to have dreams as we are inspired by our dreams. Now Modi has a dream and it’s up to all Indians to work towards the dream. This is the dream of PM of India and I don’t think any political party will differ from this. We need a PM who can inspire us and set up a goal. Personally, I think this is very difficult aim. India’s per capita GDP is roughly 3000 dollars. Despite all these years of high development China is around 13K dollar per capita GDP. India would need to go around 22K to 25 K dollar per capita GDP (in today’s team) to really become a developed country. But there is nothing wrong in having a dream and we must not under estimate the strength of India. One day we will become a developed country. This is the dream of 1.4 billion Indians.

Name: Achal

Question: Rahul Gandhi has promised to eradicate poverty from India if the Congress party is voted to power. How do you see Rahul Gandhi’s promise?
Answer: Rahul Gandhi has proved that he is the true heir of the Nehru-Gandhi family. He is using the same line that was used by his great-grandfather, grandmother, father, and mother. Her grandmother won the 1971 Lok Sabha election on the issue of eradicating poverty (Garbibi Hatao) and now Rahul Gandhi is fighting the 2024 Lok Sabha election on eradicating poverty. Rahul Gandhi has said that he would give 1 lakh rupee per year to one woman from each poor family. He said that he would finish poverty in India in one stroke with this scheme. He said that the women would continue to get the money till the time the family is below the poverty line. The fact is that Congress doesn’t know the number of poor families in India (a Congress spokesperson told this in an interview with The Wire). This is just shooting the stars with an arrow. By rough estimates, this scheme would need lakhs of crores of rupees. This is a freebee and Congress has announced many freebies (like 1 lakh rupee to every youth, making MSP a legal right, etc.). This would mean our budget deficit would rise at an alarming rate and there would be less money available for Capital expenditures like infrastructure and other development projects. It would also mean less money for education, healthcare, defense, etc. This would impact the potential economic growth of India. Such cash freebies will increase inflation in India. The supply of goods would not increase dramatically in a short span but there would be more money in the market and thus common goods would become expensive. Let’s look at a recent example - Some Western countries gave cash freebies to their people during COVID-19 period and they ended up having 10% plus inflation (compared to one or two percent inflation). Such freebies will also encourage a section of poor people to remain poor. Let’s imagine that Congress would say that a family earning less than 5 lakh rupee per annum will be classified as poor. And the day income of the family would cross 5 lakh they would not get one lakh freebies. So, there will be no incentive to increase the income (unless it increases very drastically). India needs to enable its poor people so that they can earn money and not give them cash. Will Rahul Gandhi eradicate poverty in India? The answer is No. If Rahul Gandhi does that what would be the agenda of future Congress President Rehan Rajiv Gandhi (son of Priyanka Gandhi)? He will also promise India in 2040 or 2050 that he will eradicate poverty from the country. Eradicating poverty is the family slogan of the Nehru-Gandhi family and this drama will continue for some time now.

And in a triangular fight, anything can happen and we can’t rule out all three possibilities - the DMK alliance sweeping the state, the AIADMK alliance doing relatively better and the BJP winning a couple of seats.

Lalu Yadav thinks that Pappu Yadav can emerge as a challenger to Tejashwi Yadav in Bihar after Lalu Yadav. Lalu’s health has not been good in recent years and he wants to secure the future of Tejashwi Yadav. There is no doubt that Pappu Yadav is a more grassroots and hardworking politician than Tejashwi Yadav. Congress has been contesting the Purnia seat in alliance with RJD in recent times. So, Pappu Yadav merged his party with Congress and was assured by Priyanka Gandhi that he would get the ticket from Purnia seat. Lalu Yadav has given one offer to Pappu Yadav - Merge your party with RJD and he would get a ticket from either Supaul or Madhepura. Bascially Lalu planned to make Pappu Yadav accept the leadership of Tejashwi Yadav. But Pappu Yadav resisted this and he was still not ready to accept Tejashwi Yadav as his leader. He never accepted Lalu Yadav as his leader for a long time so there is no way he would accept Tejashwi Yadav as his lever. So Lalu Yadav took Bihar Congress President Akhilesh Prasad Singh in confidence and made sure that RJD would contest three seats of Pappu Yadav’s stronghold - Purnia, Supaul, and Madhepura. Now Pappu Yadav can’t contest in any of the seats as INDIA alliance sole candidate. Let’s assume a scenario - Pappu Yadav wins Purnia seat and Lalu’s two daughters lose Patliputra and Saran. This would have been a big blow for Lalu Yadav. In RJD, Tejashwi Yadav is the ceiling point and any leader can’t emerge as a bigger leader than Tejashwi Yadav. Lalu Yadav is ready to lose some seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha election but he doesn’t want to strengthen Pappu Yadav. Now Pappu Yadav may either contest Purnia seat on a Congress ticket or as an independent against RJD candidate Bima Bharti. Winning is not a criterial for Lalu Yadav as he wants to secure the future of Tejashwi Yadav. Pappu Yadav has paid the price of his ambition to become a Yadav leader in Bihar.

Name: Achal
Question: How do you see seat sharing agreement between RJD and Congress in Bihar for 2024 Lok Sabha election?

Akhilesh Prasad Singh is an old associate of Lalu Prasad Yadav and was a Central Minister (MoS) in the First Manmohan Singh Cabinet from the RJD quota. Akhilesh Prasad Singh left RJD and joined Congress in 2010 but his equation with the Lalu family has remained intact. A few months ago, Akhilesh Prasad Singh conducted a secret deal with Lalu Yadav in which Akhilesh Prasad Singh got the Rajya Sabha seat with RJD’s help and gave up the MLC seat. Congress high command in Delhi was kept in the dark over the deal and the high command had assumed that Congress would get at least one MLC seat. The division of seats in INDIA Alliance in Bihar is - 26 seats for RJD, 9 for Congress, 3 for CPI(ML), 1 for CPI, and 1 for CPI(M). The two most popular leaders of Bihar Congress are Pappu Yadav and Kanhaiya Kumar. Akhilesh Prasad Singh has made sure that these two leaders don’t get their seats as he fears that these two leaders can overshadow him. Priyanka Gandhi had promised Pappu Yadav that he would get Purnea seat but Lalu Yadav lobbied with Akhilesh Prasad Singh to deny Pappu Yadav this seat. Congress easily gave up its claim on the Begusarai seat. Another big Congress leader in Bihar is former Delhi DGP & former Governor Nikhil Kumar (who is also the son of a former CM). His family has won the seat 8 times but this time he has been denied the chance to fight the election. Interestingly, Congress gave up Valmiki Nagar seat to take up Paschim Champaran. Last time Congress had narrowly lost Valmiki Nagar by just 22K votes and this time they would have given a very tough fight to NDA in this seat. There are rumors that Akhilesh Prasad Singh is lobbying for his son and that’s why he gave up the Valmiki Nagar seat. Congress has a realistic chance on two Muslim-dominated seats - Katihar and Kishganganj and Congress will field Muslim candidates from these two seats. Some of the very weak seats like Patna Sahib and Samastipur (SC) have been given by the alliance to Congress. This seat sharing shows that Lalu Yadav is more worried about the 2025 Assembly election and he wants to make his son Tejashwi Yadav the number one Yadav leader in Bihar. Pappu Yadav could have won Purnea seat but Lalu Yadav is ready to lose some seats to weaken Pappu Yadav. He also has denied Kanhaiya Kumar the Begusarai seat. This time, he has been doing some experiments like giving more tickets to the Kushwaha community to attract more Kushwaha votes (which is a solid vote bank of NDA). Lalu Yadav has distributed his party symbol to many RJD candidates even before the finalization of seat-sharing agreement. This is a signal to Congress that he is the boss of Bihar and Congress has no option other than becoming “C” team of RJD. NDA has announced candidates on 37 seats and INDIA alliance has not announced even a single candidate. Even though many RJD candidates have privately received symbol from RJD. As of now, it’s an advantage for NDA in Bihar because of the arrogance of Lalu Yadav.

Name: Achal
Question: Is Kejriwal's “government from jail” justified?
Answer: Arvind Kejriwal has made many records in Indian politics. Now, he has become the first CM to run the Government from jail. Indian constitution doesn’t stop a CM from running the Government from jail because our founding fathers were not as innovative and imaginative as Arvind Kejriwal. Arvind Kejriwal has gone beyond the established moral norms that a CM would resign before going to jail.
