Name: Achal
Question: Is the launch of so many Vande Bharat express has been a blunder made by the Modi Govt?
Answer: Yes, Vande Bharat Express is a blunder by Modi Government because certain section of Indians don’t like improvement in Indian Railways. Does Indian Railways have problem? Yes, Indian Railways have lot of problems. Any railway system with roughly a billion plus population using railways would struggle to keep the railways afloat. Have you ever talked with a German or a French or a Dutch about condition of their railways ? They routinely complain about the state of their railways. In Germany people joke about the state and punctuality of railways. India has lot of space to improve railways but where is the money? In this money, you will get this much. Nothing is free in the world and Railways needs money a lot of money. A big section of tracks and bridges are more than century old. The train fares in India is very low compared to road transport. From my hometown, non-AC & normal bus charges Rs. 200 to 250 to go to Patna and the train fare is around Rs 70. Indians must learn to pay money to get the service. Yes, a section of passenger trains and sleeper class trains must be maintained. But there should be improvement in services for those who can pay it. India is perhaps the only country in top 10 economies with no world class trains. Vanda Bharat is a small step towards having global standard train services. Now, please don’t start crying that a big section of Indians can’t afford Vande Bharat trains (the usual Leftist liberal point). Yes, ever bigger section of Indians can’t afford air travel. Does it mean that Indian should not invest in Airport infrastructure ? There is no Vande Bharat in my area in Bihar (Barauni - Muzaffarpur, Barauni-Darbhanga section) and there is huge demand for the train in my area. Do you stop doing everything in life if you have diabetes or hypertension? No you tray to live with that disease and work as usual. Let us be very clear - Indian Railway stations and trains are dirty because we Indians make them dirty. This is a generational problem and it will improve in coming years. Many of our tracks are running at full capacity and running additional trains are difficult. We need to lay third or even fourth line is some of the busy routes. Let me give an example - You can run hundreds of special trains between Bihar and Delhi during Diwali/Chhath Puja time but you can’t solve the congestion in that route. It will take decades to solve the fundamental problems of Indian railways but it doesn’t mean that we stop introducing world class trains. I have been travelling in trains since I was born and the condition of trains in India has improves vastly but there are still a lot of room for improvement. We need more Vanda Bharat trains in India as many sections are still not served by the Vande Bharat trains.

Name: Achal
Question: Is Kejriwal’s party, the AAM Aadmi Party, finished?
Answer: No, Arvind Kejriwal’s AAP is not finished. The party seems to be down but it is still a very strong political party. In Indian political history, never a regional party has ruled two states (when AAP won Punjab it was a regional party). Only national parties like Congress, BJP, CPM, and defunct national parties (Like Janta Party, and Janta Dal) have ruled two states. This may remain one of the greatest achievements of Arvind Kejriwal he has won two states - Delhi and Punjab. His control in the Delhi assembly is so strong that the party has won more than 60 seats (out of 70 seats) in two consecutive elections. AAP is a party that was born out of a movement and it portrayed itself as a different and clean party. AAP used to claim that they were the “cleanest” political party. In the last few years, AAP has lost that moral high ground and it has become another usual political party. Thus AAP has lost its main capital of being an honest party. Irrespective of the outcome of the liquor scam, Kejriwal’s image took a massive hit when the reports came out that Kejriwal had used more than 52 cr. in the renovation of CM’s house. Now, the top leadership of AAP - Kejriwal, Sisodia, and Sanjay Singh are in jail. This has hurt the brand image of AAP. Image Source - Indian Express But this doesn’t mean that AAP is finished. In India, many leaders have faced corruption charges and some like Lalu Yadav have been convicted on charges of corruption. But their politics has remained the same and somehow they have managed to keep their political relevance. If a Lalu can remain politically relevant then why can’t Arvind Kejriwal remain politically relevant? But there is one weak point of Kejriwal - Kejriwal doesn't have a permanent dedicated vote bank like Lalu Yadav. In case Congress can revive itself in Delhi and Punjab then it will hurt AAP. Muslims and poor voters of Delhi can dump AAP and go to Congress the same way they dumped Congress and went into AAP’s fold. But I don’t see Congress climbing the charts rapidly in Delhi. So, AAP’s future is secure in Delhi in the near and medium term. What can go wrong in the 2025 Delhi Assembly election for AAP? Even in defeat AAP will remain the main opposition party in Delhi and will secure more votes than Congress. The corruption charges against Kejriwal will hurt AAP’s growth outside Delhi and Punjab. The AAP’s story as a “clean and different” party is over and it may remain as normal political party like RJD SP or Congress.

Name: Achal
Question: Will the arrest of Kejriwal prove to be a boomreng for BJP in LS elections? Will AAP be successful to establish this as a revenge action from BJP in voter's mind? Will the victim card work?
Answer: Kejriwal’s image has taken a hit in last few years. The biggest blow to his image came from reports that he has spent 52 cr. on renovation of his house. The 2024 Lok Sabha election is not Kejriwal’s main fight and his real election the 2025 assembly election.

Name: Achal
Question: What are the chances of Annamalai winning the Coimbatore parliamentary seat?
Answer: Coimbatore Lok Sabha seat is a very tough seat for BJP Tamil Nadu President K Annamalai but he can win the seat also. Let us look at the history of Coimbatore Lok Sabha seat - This shows that the DMK-led alliance has had the upper hand since 1999 and the DMK alliance has won the seat 4 times out of 5 times. BJP was with DMK in 1999 and with AIADMK in 1998. But DMK on its symbol has not won the seat since 1996 and they have been allocating the seats to their allies. Most of the time, AIADMK and DMK had given this seat to national parties and in the last 6 election, they faced each other only once in 2014. But the last assembly election showed a different picture - AIADMK alliance (when BJP was part of the alliance) swept all 6 assembly seats of this Lok Sabha constituency. Not only this, DMK alliance lost all 10 assembly seats in the Coimbatore district. The city has remained a bastion of AIADMK in the last few assembly elections but the DMK alliance had fared better in the Lok Sabha elections. Let us look at the last two election results - BJP as a member of the AIADMK alliance lost the seat in 2019 but they came second in 2014 when they were leading a third front in the state. This time DMK has taken the seat from its alliance partner CPI(M) and the seat will see a three-cornered contest. AIADMK has given the ticket to Singai G. Ramachandran, head of the party’s IT wing. Singai G. Ramachandran is the son of a former AIADMK MLA and is a new face in electoral politics. and DMK has given the ticket to its Coimbatore district president Ganapathy Rajkumar. Ganapathy Rajkumar is the former mayor of the city and has spent decades in AIADMK and he joined DMK in 2020. Both DMK and AIADMK candidates are good & strong candidates. But BJP also thinks that they have a chance in Coimbatore. There are many reasons - K Annamalai is their state president and strongest candidate, the 1998 bomb blast, their relatively strong base in the district, a good number of North Indian presence in the district due to the textile industry, etc. In 1998, there were bomb blasts in the city by Islamic terrorists of Al Ummah. The idea of terrorists was to kill L K Advani but 58 innocent people were killed by Jehadi terrorists. And Coimbatore was one of the earliest seats in Tamil Nadu which was won by the BJP. K Annamalai also has the blessing of Sadhguru who is based out of Coimbatore. PM Modi did his first political activity (after the announcement of poll dates for the 2024 Lok Sabha election) in Coimbatore. DMK Govt. had denied the permission to BJP to hold Modi’s roadshow in Coimbatore but BJP got relief from the High Court. It is certain that many big BJP leaders will campaign for Annamalai. Coimbatore remains the most hopeful seat for the BJP in Tamil Nadu along with the Kanyakumari seat. BJP has also created a third front with PMK, TMC (M) and AMMK. In a tough triangular fight, a 35–38% vote share can be enough in Coimbatore. Annamalai is very capable of getting 35% vote share in the seat and the same can be said for DMK and AIADMK candidates. Coimbatore will see a mouth-watering contest in the election. Let be very clear that Annamalai is not a pushover candidate and most likely he will be in the main fight (i.e. top 2).

Name: Achal
Question: Bahubali politician from Bihar Pappu Yadav has joined the Congress party. DO you think that Pappu Yadav can revive Congress in Bihar?
Answer: Congress is thinking that Pappu Yadav can help Congress to revive in Seemanchal (North - Eastern part of Bihar which has a significant Muslim population). Pappu Yadav is a very controversial figure in Bihar. Pappu Yadav was involved in a bitter gangster rivalry with Anand Mohan in Seemanchal in the 1980s and 1990s. Many people have lost their lives in that rivalry. Pappu Yadav was the leader of the Yadav gang and Anand Mohan was the leader of the Rajput gang. Pappu Yadav was even sentenced in the murder of Communist MLA and his political rival Ajit Sarkar but was later acquitted by Patna High Court. There were many criminal cases against Pappu Yadav but he was acquitted in many cases due to a lack of evidence. As per the 2019 poll affidavit, there were 32 criminal cases pending against Pappu Yadav. It is believed that Ranjita Ranjan is close to Priyanka Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi played an important role in bringing Pappu Yadav in BJP’s fold. There is no doubt that Pappu Yadav has a fan following in many Lok Sabha seats - Purnea, Madhrpura, Supaul etc. This means that Pappu Yadav may get a Congress ticket from Purnea. In the last few years, Pappu Yadav has been active in the whole of Bihar and he used to visit everywhere after any incident he is known for helping Biharis in Delhi (like helping in getting admission in hospitals). Pappu Yadav will certainly boost Congress in Seemanchal. Congress’s sole MP is from that region (Kishanganj). But Pappu Yadav is a party hopper and his past may alienate many voters away from Congress. Congress can at least double its tally in Bihar with help of Pappu Yadav. It is assumed that Congress will win Muslim-dominated Kishanganj seat and now Congress has chance in Purnea against JD(U). But the Purnea Lok Sabha seat has changed sinch Pappu Yadav won the seat in 1999 as an independent candidate. BJP won twice in 2004 and 2009 and JD(U) surprisingly won the seat in 2014 contesting alone. So, Purnea will see a mouth-watering contest between Santosh Kushwaha and Pappu Yadav in the 2024 Lok Sabha seat. Pappu Yadav is still 56 years of age despite being in politics for 24 years but this is a stop-gap arrangement for Congress revival. Congress needs to work hard to create a base in Bihar and importing Bahubali politicians may help in one seat. Pappu Yadav may not help Congress in revival of Congress but can help Congress win an extra seat in Bihar.

Name: Achal
Question: What is the retirement age for politicians in India?
Answer: There is no retirement age in Indian politics. Many politicians have remained in active politics in their 90s. In India, the majority of the politicians (from non-political family backgrounds) gain prominent positions in their 50s and 60s. There are some exceptions but a 55-year-old politician is considered to be a young politician. Rahul Gandhi (54 years of age) and Akhilesh Yadav (50 years), Yogi Adityanath (51 years) are considered to be young politicians in India. In India, the public hardly trusts a 30 or 40-year-old politician (when he/she is not from a political family). We have seen very very few politicians becoming CM of a state before 40 years of age. In the 2019 election, only 13% of our MPS were below 40 and the majority of them were from political families (with some exceptions like Tejaswi Surya) and 47% of our MPs were above 55 years of age. Once one get power its very hard to let that power go. This is not just with politics but with our families as well. In India, almost every aspect of the life of a young person was decided by the elders in the family - starting from the subjects in education to marriage to job to house. So, that has been carried forward to politics and as the new generation is making more and more independent decisions it will reflect in politics sooner or later. We will see such changes in the next two or three decades. Let’s see some of the recent examples of active politicians over 90 years of age - But these are rare cases as the life expectancy of Indians is around 71 years age. Till 200, life expectance was in the early 60s. So, we see so many Indian political leaders in the 70s. Only those who are healthy remain active in their 80s and very few in their 90s. The majority of Indian politicians are from 55 to 70 years of age. I hope that in the coming decades, we will see many more politicians assuming political posts in their 40s and 50s.

Name: Achal
Question: Why are opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi saying the electoral bond is a scam?

Rupee donations as electoral bonds between 2109 and 2024 but still claim that the bond scheme is a scam. Their thinking is that every political party should receive the same amount of money irrespective of performance. BJP received most of the donations because they are the number one party in India. If Congress crosses the 272 mark on its own in the upcoming 2024 election, the party will start receiving more money than Congress. If Rahul Gandhi has the guts then his party must return 1423 cr. Rupee donations and then call it a scam. Congress (mostly the Gandhi family) has ruled India for over 5 decades and they were very successful politically. One of the reasons for Congress’s success was its ability to outspend other parties (the same thing BJP is doing now). It is believed that the Congress party was very successful in collecting the money. The “suitcase method” (black money in cash) used to be a very popular means of political funding. There are allegations that Congress used to get funds via Trusts/Foundations like the National Herald, The Rajiv Gandhi Charitable Trust (RGCT), numerous scams etc. Let’s see some of examples of fundings by Congress This article is from 1984 where the writer Kuldip Nayar alleges that Congress party has developed a new way of funding apart from asking donations from industrialists - Cut money in Goverment purchases from abroad. Yes Bank founder Rana Kapoor alleged that Gandhi’s forced him to buy a 2 cr. painting from the Gandhi family. License Raj was one of the best ways to “extract” donations from industrialists. The problem is that now Congress receives way less money than the BJP. Congress rules 3 states and it has around 10% Lok Sabha seats. On the other hand, BJP has 17 states and 55% of Lok Sabha seats. The BJP will attract more donations because it’s the number one party. You can’t claim that IPL is a scam just because players like Kohli and MSD revive way more money than Piyush Chawla or Manish Pandey. In IPL irrespective of the salary, all players in playing 11 get their chance to perform. The same happens in politics - irrespective of funding and spending all political parties have an equal chance to attract votes. Non-BJP parties received 53% of the electoral bonds the the share of non-NDA parties would be around 47–48% and INDIA alliance share may be around 40%. So let INDIA alliance parties return thousands of crores received as electoral bonds then call it a scam. You can’t have both ways. Let’s take an example - Dravidian parties even didn’t spare an IPL team. CSK also paid donations to Dravidian parties in Tamil Nadu.

Name: Achal
Question: What are your thoughts on the scandal involving Electoral Bonds in India?
Answer: Electoral Bonds were a step towards cleaner political donation in India. This was not perfect but way better than previous cash & black money transfers. All political parties and political movements run on money. Mahatma Gandhi had so many close "industrialist" friends. Gandhi ji could not have built so many big Ashrams without donations and he spent his last days in the palatial "Birla House" in Delhi. Since independence, Indian politics has been running with cash and black money transfers from industrialists and mafias. All big industrialists used to give cash to political parties. Electoral Bond was a scheme in which companies/individuals could donate white money to political parties. This money was shown in the books of both donors and receivers. All political parties were required to mention the amount received via these bonds to the Election Commission. And on the other side, this money was also on the books of companies. The Electoral Bond bill was passed by the Indian Parliament in 2017 and was implemented in 2018. Now Supreme Court has struck down this law. As per the bill, the Indian state had promised the donors that their names would not come in public. But now their names are in public and this means no industrial house will ever believe the Indian state shortly and give "white money" to politicians. Now let us analyze the disclosure of the Electoral Bonds - BJP has the lion’s share of these bonds because they are in power in the Centre and rule more than half of Indian states. Yes, like every Indian, our Jat Sikh farmers have all the rights of protest. But this protest must be peaceful and they must not encircle and choke our National Capital. They have all the rights to demand MSP or anything being citizen of a democratic India. I am not going into maths and economics of demands of farmers. It is up to the government to decide on those demands and other Indians to think about such demands. I come from a farming family in Bihar and my family is not part of such protest. It is wrong to say that this is a farmer's protest, but this is a protest of Punjabi Jat farmers.

Name: Achal
Question: Will Arvind Kejriwal join the BJP?
Answer: Let’s assume that humans have invented aTime Machine. Let’s also assume that an India (who was aware about Indian politics) from 2011–13 travels to 2024 with the Time Machine. He/She will be shocked to see AAP aligning with Congress and Kejriwal is an alliance with leaders like Sonia Gandhi, Sharad Pawar, Lalu Yadav, Akhilesh Yadav, Stalin etc. Kejriwal’s politics was built on anti-Congress and anti-dynasty politics but there is no place of morality in politics. India have seen so many un-natural political alliance like Congress - Lalu Yadav, Congress - Mulayam Singh Yadav, BJP- Sukhram , Congress - TDP, BJP-PDP, Congress - Communists etc. Nothing is impossible in politics and one can’t rule out a tie up between Kejriwal and BJP. But as of now I don’t see a tie up between AAP and BJP in future.

Name: Achal
Question: When will Kejriwal be the P.M. of India?
Answer: The answer is very simple. Kejriwal will become the PM of India the day he will have support of 272 MPs in Lol Sabha. But now you have to find out when 272 MPs would support Kejriwal.

Name: Achal
Question: Which party will make the biggest difference in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections?
Answer: It’s obvious that Congress would make the biggest difference in the upcoming Lok Sabha election. Yes, Modi has done so many things and promises to do many things. A big section of Indians are die heat supporter of Modi. But still Modi has ruled India for almost a decade. It’s the Congress party which time and again demonstrates that why India should keep voting for Modi. Rahul Gandhi till date remains the second most vote catcher for BJP after Modi. In all these years in opposition, Congress has failed to present an alternative model for governance. Their past performances have been so weak that Indian public is not able to take promises of Congress at face value. Let’s take an example - Congress is promising to give more space to OBC and the fact that Congress has been the most anti-OBC party in India. So, OBCs don’t take Congress promise of more representation seriously.

Name: Achal
Question: What do you think of Siddaramaiah's confidence of the Congress winning a minimum of 20 Lok Sabha seats in Karnataka?
Answer: It’s quite natural that Karnataka CM Siddaramiah is saying that Congress would win minimum 20 Lok Sabha seats in the state. Siddaramiah has been facing heat from his Deputy CM DK Shivkumar and he had to deliver result in the 2024 Lol Sabha election. If Congress fails to win minimum of half Lol Sabha seats in Karnataka then both Siddaramiah and DSK (party state President) would face the heat. There was a close door deal between Siddaramiah, DKS and the Gandhi family under which DKS agreed to give up his claim on the post of CM. So, in case Siddaramiah would appear weak then the DKS may try to take advantage of the situation and may ask for the post of CM. Almost all pre poll survery is giving NDA 20 plus seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. This may be demoralizing for Congress workers. So, CM Siddaramiah may be trying to boost the morale of Congress workers ahead of the election claiming that Congress would win 20 plus seats in the Lok Sabha election.

Name: Achal
Question: What do you think about Lalu Prasad's remark that "doors are always open" for Nitish Kumar?
Answer: Lalu Yadav is a seasoned and a shrewd politician. His last remaining single aim in his remaining life is to see his son Tejashwi Yadav as CM of Bihar. He knows that Tejashwi Yadav can’t become CM of Bihar (in current political scenarios) without the support of Nitish Kumar. The deal between Nitish, Lalu and Congress in 2022 was that Nitish would shift to national politics and Tejashwi would become CM of Bihar. But now the deal broke and Nitish is back in NDA. Nitish Kumar is an alliance hopper who likes to keep a communication channel open with opposition. Lalu Yadav’s state confirmed that Nitish may be sending some hints to both BJP and RJD. Nitish wants more bargaining power in negotiations with BJP for Lol Sabha seats. Lalu hopes to keep a channel of negotiation open with Nitish Kumar. Such statements keep Bihar politics interesting.

Name: Achal
Question: Why is Rahul Gandhi raising questions over PM Modi’s OBC status?
Answer: Rahul Gandhi has said that Narendra Modi was not born as an OBC and he included his caste in OBC list when he became CM. Let’s talk about some of the points - The list of OBC is complex in India. Some of the casts are classified as OBC in some state and as General in some states and it’s very confusing. Let’s take an example - Baniya caste is OBC in Bihar and they are general in many North Indian states. As per our law, Narendra Modi is an OBC. Based on various criteria’s the OBC list gets expanded. Rahul Gandhi’s statement shows his desperation. No one takes Rahul Gandhi’s so called OBC pitch seriously and the fun fact is that Congress party has been fundamentally anti-OBC in its most of its existence.

Name: Achal
Question: Sonia Gandhi has dumped Rae Barely Lok Sabha seat and chose Rajasthan for her Rajya Sabha seat. What’s your opinion about this?
Answer: There are many reasons that Sonia Gandhi has preferred Rajya Sabha over contesting Lok Sabha election. This may be a smart move for Congress but this has sent wrong signals to the party workers. When the top leadership takes Rajya Sabha route than Lok Sabha spite it sends a wrong signal to the party rank and file. This decision sends a message that Congress can’t win seats in North India on its own (however Congress May win some seats). This is a demoralizing news for Congress workers. It seems that Congress high commands has acknowledged the potential defeat in 2024 and they are fighting to increase their seat tally. Gandhi’s have never taken Rjaya Savha route. Three Gandhis (Indira, Sanjay and Rahul) have lost Lok Savha elections but they had not taken Rajya Sabha route. This decision sums up the state of Congress for the 2024 Lok Sabha election.

Name: Achal
Question: Rahul Gandhi has promised to remove 50% cap for caste-based reservation. Do you think that this move will help the Congress party in the 2024 Lok Sabha election?
Answer: Rahul Gandhi has a unique talent for losing vote banks and annoying vote bank. The traditional vote bank of Congress had three pillars - General casts, Dalits and Muslims. General casts have shifted to BJP from Congress, but Congress still has some support left among General casts. Rahul Gandhi’s demand of caste census had affected Congress prospect adversely in Hindi belt elections in 2023. And now, Rahul Gandhi is openly talking about breaching the caste-based reservation cap of 50%. This would mean that Congress would lose a big chunk of its vote among general casts. Congress hopes to gain votes among OBCs & Dalits with this move. But this may not happen. Powerful OBCs casts have their own regional parties and a big section of OBCs support PM Modi. The thinking of an educated OBC voter from an urban area is similar to the thinking of a general category voter and we all know that BJP has a big upper hand in urban areas. On top of it, PM Modi is the biggest ever OBC political leader in India. The OBCs have become flag bearer of Hindutwa politics along with general category. Our OBC brothers and sisters take the same pride in nationalism as any other Indian. Do Rahul Gandhi & Gandhi family represent the aspirations of OBC? The answer is no. OBC wants to see their own face in public office and the so-called “Jenaudhari” brahmin Rahul Gandhi can’t capture the imagination of OBCs. We must remember that general cast (Rajput) leaders like V P Singh (who implemented Mandal comission) and Arjun Singh (who implemented OBC reservation in education) failed to attract OBC voters. A few months ago, Congress appointed 12 general secretaries and only one of them was OBC. Rahul Gandhi is crying foul that very few OBCs are secretaries of departments in Central Government. The fact is that OBC reservation came into effect in early 1990s and till now most of the secretaries are before 1992 batch. And before that OBC IAS officers were classified as GENERAL. It was COngress which sat on Mandal Commission report for almost a decade. In this process, Congress is losing general category votes without attracting OBC votes. PM Modi’s strongest vote bank is General category despite the fact that Modi is OBC. Modi doesn’t overplay the OBC card. He rarely says that he is OBC and say this on limited occasions to get political mileage. Politics is an art where you need to attract a group without alienating other group. Caste based political parties like RJD, BSP, SP are trying hard to get a chunk of general category votes but Congress is alienating general category votes. This is the era of OBC politics and many states - Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Jharkhand, Telangana, Haryana, Chhattisgarh have already breached the 50% mark. The general category understands that reservation may increase but they can go against parties which openly talk about increasing reservation. Rahul Gandhi needs to play smart politics, otherwise he may have spend many more years in opposition.

Name: Achal
Question: How is village life not better?
Answer: Village life is romanticized in India to be better by urban people, but reality is far from it. I come from a semi-urban place in Bihar and I have a lot of relatives in nearby villages. I have seen the struggle of villages closely. In the last few decades, I have seen a lot of deaths in my extended family because of a lack of medical facilities. Some of the examples are - One of my aunts died of complications out of pregnancy , one of my uncles died because he could not get proper medical attention after a heart attack (we had to take him to Patna and he died in the 3 hours' journey), my fathers disease was wrongly diagnosed and he was unnecessary given a lot of antibiotics for a year. For villagers, everything is a challenge. Just a few years ago, any bank work used to take the whole day. They would not get many items in local shops and the education quality is very, very bad. On top of that there are a lot of caste issues and unnecessary competition. If I leave my job today and start a business in my area and if it becomes successful, many of my neighbours would lodge many false cases to pull me down. In my area, people spend more time in thinking ways to pull you down rather than their development. The quarrel and tension because of land disputes is very very common. If our family doesn’t get a new land related tension a week, then they think that week was good. And don’t talk about the level of education system. Most of the villages lack proper drinking water (Connectivity, sanitiation and electricity condition have improved in the last few years) . These are some reasons that almost every small or marginal farmer or labour or someone doing some work (like carpentry, construction work etc) want that their children should move out the village. Yes, there are some advantages of living in villages - less pollution, more space, fresh food & vegetables etc. but there are a lot of disadvantages as well. And we must remember that large amount of wealth is created in urban areas, not in villages.

Name: Achal
Question: Who is behind the Opposition Alliance demise as one leader after the other are saying goodbye to the Mahagathbandhan?
Answer: It seems that the the alliance called INDIA may be reduced to its previous version called UPA plus one or two allies like Uddhav’s Shiv Sena. The biggest reason for unreveling for INDIA alliance has been Rahul Gandhi and Congress. The most important leader of Congress - Rahul Gandhi, is missing in action with his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra. In the time of start of the war, you need your main general to be at headquarter planning for the war. But the General of Congress is missing. And the next in command, Mallikarjun Kharge doesn’t have the authority to take decision. Kharge has to take advice (or permission) from Rahul Gandhi on alliance talks and persuading allies. On top of that, most of the Congress leaders are busy in making Rahul’s yatra a success. Congress had delivered something (convenor post of the alliance) to Nitish Kumar and it failed. Congress leaders have been constantly attacking Mamata Banarjee in West Bengal and Rahul Gandhi has not personally reached out to Mamata Banarjee. The absence of Rahul Gandhi is making allies jittery. If Rahul would have talked with Akhilesh, then he would have secured more than 11 seats. And the alliances in other states are not coming through. In Bihar, RJD has been slow in seat sharing talks. There is a feeling among politicians that INDIA alliance can’t defeat BJP. This means that regional parties have to save their own base as they think that they have not much to gain out of the opposition alliance. The central leader of the alliance Rahul Gandhi is faltering as the commander of the alliance and thus INDIA Alliance is looking weak.

Name: Achal
Question: Is a Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) coup against Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar (Janata Dal United) in the offing?
Answer: No, The JD(U) is firmly behind Nitish Kumar and there are very remote chance that RJD can break JD(U). The other is true. BJP and JD(U) are in touch with Congress MLAs and the Congress party has shifted its MLAs to Hyderabad to save the party in Bihar. JD(U) has 45 MLAs and RJD will have to break 30 MLAs. If less than 30 MLAs revolt, these MLAs would lose their seat. NDA would remove the RJD’s assembly speaker - Awadh Bihari Chaudhary first. Once the speaker is gone, RJD can’t do anything. Even if RJD has speaker and they break JD(U) with less than 30 MLAs and Nitish fails to prove majority, the Governor would not call RJD to form the Government. This would mean a fresh election in Bihar. As per some rumors, Lalan Singh would have broken JD(U). But Lalan Singh has been a close friend of Nitish Kumar and in 2010, when Lalan Singh ha revolted against Nitish Kumar, he didn’t break the party. BJP had great hopes with RCP Singh in 2022, but RCP could not break a single MLA of JD(U). Yes, a few MLAs may change the party (as usual) close to the election date, but no JD(U) MLA would like to sacrifice his/her seat for RJD. Image Source - PTI It's the social media team of Lalu Yadav and Congress party which has floated the rumor that RJD will destabilize the Nitish Kumar Government. This is a time when both Lalu Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav are facing serious charges in “Land for Job” scam. We need to move over social media speculations and think about reality.

Name: Achal
Question: Who is Nitish Kumar?
Answer: Nitish Kumar is like an enigma machine in Indian politics. No one knows what is going on in his mind. Before his last flip, Lalu Yadav went to meet Nitish Kumar with Tejashwi Yadav. Nitish assured the Lalu family that he would not flip. In August 2022, he had assured Amit Shah on the phone that he would not leave NDA and he left NDA withing a few days. Nowadays, no one in Indian politics takes the statement of Nitish Kumar on its face value. Nitish Kumar is perhaps one of the smartest politician in India. He neither has a big dedicated vote bank nor he comes from a numerical superior caste. He is also not a mass politician. But he is still CM of Bihar since 2005 (except for a small break). Bihar has only one truth these days: Nitish Kumar will be the CM. Nitish is constant and BJP & RJD are variables. He is acceptable to both BJP and RJD. He chooses and rejects BJP & RJD on his will. His door is always open for both parties and he is comfortable with both parties. He was the first one to work on the oppositional alliance called INDIA. He travelled all over the country and hosted the first meeting of alliance in Patna. But now he had dumped the alliance. Nitish Kumar has one goal - to remain CM of Bihar and get a national role if possible. He doesn’t let morality or ego come in between his goal. He is the only politician who resigns to take oath again. Image Source - India Today Let's be fair to Nitish Kumar. His first term (2005–10) was the best time for Bihar in the last few decades. But he lost the way and Nitish got addicted to the CM chair. He has no moral values, but morality has no place in politics. History will not treat Nitish Kumar fairly because of his flip-flops, despite some good work because it has destroyed his own image with his actions.

Name: Achal
Question: Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren has lodged FIR against ED officials under SC/ST act for raiding his Delhi house and spreading so-called fake news against him. Do you think that this is a grave misuse of SC/St act?
Answer: This is one of the best examples of misuse of SC/ST act and it has come from one of the highest constitutional post in India - a sitting Chief Minister. Enforcement Directorate has been investing a case of money laundering case inked to an alleged land deal in Jharkhand against Former Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren (he was the CM till a few days ago and then he resigned before going to jail). ED officials raided Hemant Soren’s Delhi house and claimed that they siezed an expensive car, money and some documents. As per ED, a sitting CM in India went untracable for sometime. Later Hemant Soren was seen in Ranchi where he resigned and was arrested. Before his arrest, Hemant Soren lodged FIR against ED officials (from their Ranchi office) in Ranchi under Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. In this case, one can’t bail anbd one has to go to jail just because of FIR. In the FIR Soren alleged that the ED conducted the search operation at his residence in the national capital to “harass and malign him and his entire community”. Hemant Soren was CM when the FIr was lodged and now ED offficials are facing imminent arrest. There are corruption charges against an individual and it has nothing to do with tribal community or any caste. We don’t know the outcome of the money laundering case as the final court verdict will take some time. There are chances that the allegation on Hemant Soren may be true or false. But no one can justify SC/ST act against agencies just becaus ethey are investingating a case againt you. This opens a floodgate as people may start filing against agencies like police, ED, CBI, vigilance department or any other department in case these agencies start any investigating against the person. It is unfortunate that we still witness atrocities against SCs & STs in some part of India and this must stop. But at the same many people claim that SC/ST act is misused. The time has come where we must stop the mis use of SC/ST act and also ensure that no atrocities are comiiuted against SCs & STs.

Name: Achal
Question: Why are Indian leftist liberals supporting convicted politician Lalu Prasad Yadav?
Answer: As a Bihari, my blood boils when I see someone outside Bihar praises and defend Lalu Yadav. Yes, Lalu Yadav has its own vote bank and they love him in the state, but it is strange that Leftist Liberals living outside Bihar are praising & hailing Lalu Yadav. Let me narrate my story. When I was growing up as a child in the 1990s, there was no electricity for 5 years despite being living in a notified “urban area”. And when electricity supply resumed, there was not a single evening with undisrupted power supply. Till 12th (early 2000s), I studied in a kerosene lamp every evening when the rest of India was booming because of economic liberalization. When I appeared for 12th exam one friend (who was rich) never came to give exam and he secured 75% marks. I had seen my relatives spending the whole night on railway station because they were fearful of going to their home, which was just 1–2 KM away from the railway station. I had seen educational sessions delayed by many years, i.e. if you were doing 3 year graduation (say 1995–98) then you would get your final graduation result in 2000 or 2001. Every alternate day, I used to read the news of kidnapping, and rich children around me were always worried. I was literally forced to leave Bihar to study outside the state as the Lalu era had destroyed the education system in the state. Now my state has gradually become the state of old people (mainly of middle-class people). When I look back, I found that all my cousins have left Bihar. Our family will lose the connection with Bihar in one generation. This is the story of every other house in Bihar. Migration is the natural phenomenon, but such mass migration is rarely seen. If you want to know more about the Lalu era, please go and ask millions of lonely parents of Bihar that what does it means to live lonely without children. Lalu’s 15 year rule destroyed two-three generations of Biharis. The Congress & Socialist rule in earlier decades was also not good, but Lalu literally destroyed Bihar. Let’s give an example - When Bengaluru and Hyderabad were building IT companies, Bihar was building non functional “Charwaha Schools”. This was the Lalu era. Now Lau’s supporters would argue about social justice. The 1980s and 1990s were the era of Social Justice in whole India and that was the time of rise of OBCs in North Indian politics. With or without Lalu Social justice would have swept Bihar. There was no Lalu Yadav in MP or Rajasthan, but social justice happened in those states too. Social Justice doen’t mean that you destroy almost every institution of the state and take it backwards. Lalu Yadav is a convicted politician in many cases of fodder scam and the allegations in Land for Job scam are very serious. How can anyone defend a convicted criminal who has never lived in Bihar?

Name: Achal
Question: What is the biggest weakness of Bihar CM Nitish Kumar in Bihar politics?
Answer: I am a critic of Nitish Kumar but at the same time I praise Nitish Kumar’s first tenure (2005–10). In my opinion, the biggest weakness of Nitish Kumar is lack of a good social media strategy. On 28th Jan 2024, Nitish Kumar flipped again and took oath as CM for the record 9th time. RJD’s social media warriors created a narrative on social media that Tejashwi Yadav was the real “Vikas Purush” (developmental oriented leader). They started hailing Tejashwi Yadav as savior of not only Bihar, but for India. On top of that Congress and Leftist Liberal lobby joined hands with RJD warriors and started attacking Nitish Kumar and praising Tejashwi Yadav. Anti-Nitish block also created a fake narrative that Tejashwi would become CM after breaking JD(U). On the other hand, RW & BJP supporters also attacked Nistish Kumar and BJP as they were not happy with BJP’s decision to go with Nitish Kumar. So there was no group on social media to defend Nitish Kumar and his image got hammered on social media. I am not defending Nitish Kumar and he is the “Paltu Ram” of Bihar politics. But at the same time, Nitish Kumar is much better that Lalu Yadav and his family. Yesterday, Lalu Yadav was questioned by ED in Land for Job scam for 9 hours. Leftist Liberal media, Congress and RJD supporters tried to create a narrative that he is the real saviour of Bihar and Indian politics. The reality is that Lalu Yadav has been convicted in many corruption cases of the fodder scam and there are serious allegations against him in the land for Job scam. Nitish Kumar needs a social media strategy. There is hardly any voice of JD(U) on social media. This is hurting Nitish Kumar’s image. The other fact is that Nitish Kumar has a vote bank in EBCs apart from his own caste. EBCs are the marginalized OBCs whose individual numbers are small and they are also not vocal on social media. If you see the OBC point of view on social media, big OBC casts like the Yadav community dominate it and EBCs lack proper representation. Nitish Kumar is still an old school politician and one reason for his diminishing popularity is that he has not understood the modern politics. Nitish Kumar is a weak but very smart politician. He is nearing the end of his long political journey. I would like to thank him for his excellent first tenure, but he has played his own part in destroying Bihar after his first tenure. If JD(U) has to survive beyond 2025, they need to come up with a good social media strategy.

Name: Achal
Question: Why has Mamata Banerjee decided to contest the upcoming Lok Sabha polls independently in the state?
Answer: Mamata Banarjee has been virtually forced by Congress to announce that the TMC would contest the 2024 Lok Sabha election on its own. On the other hand, TMC was also not enthusiastic about alliance up with Congress - Mamata Banarjee has said many times that regional parties should fight BJP in their own turf and Congress should concetrate on stats where the party is strong. Congress had to chose between Left front and TMC & Congress have not clearly decided on this issue. Its the last week of Jan and the election dates wuld be annouced in a few weeks. So, TMC has declared that it would fight election on its own. there may still be pre-poll alliance between Congress and TMC in West bengal but the chances are very slim.

Name: Achal
Question: Do you think the NDA may sweep Bihar in the 2024 Lok Sabha election with Nitish Kumar?
Answer: NDA has a very good chance of winning 35 to 38 Lok Sabha seats (out of 40) in Bihar after the return of Nitish Kumar. Let us look at the 2019 Lok Sabha elections - NDA had 53.25% vote share and the MGB (now INDI Alliance) had less than 31% vote share. Now Left front (most important CPIML) is with them. So just by 2019’s number they have 33% votes. Let us look at the margin of NDA’s victory. There were only three seats where the victory margin was less than 50K. Congress, BJP and JD(U) had won those seats. NDA had won 3 seats with 4 Lakh plus margin, 4 seats with 3 lakh plus margin and 18 seats with 2 Lakh plus margin. So, the NDA starts the 2024 election at a very high base. Yes, there was Pulwama in 2019 but this time there is Ram Mandir. Narendra Modi remains very popular in Bihar and BJP’s organizational base in 2024 is stronger than that of 2019. On the other hand, RJD and CPI(ML) have also become stronger compared to 2019. Some parties like JD(U) and Congress, have declined compared to 2019. If you look at the Nitish cabinet and the caste combination of NDA, its very clear. NDA would like to create this caste coalition - General casts, prominent OBC casts like Koeri and Kurmi, MBCs and Mahadalits. NDA also has Dalit leaders like Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi. Chirag Paswan has a small but very committed vote bank in every district. On the other hand, INDI Allaince core vote bank is - Yadav, Mulsims and some OBC/MBC casts. Some Yadavs do vote for BJP in Lok Sabha elections and this is evident from victory of Yadav leaders like Ram Kripal Yadav and Nityanad Rai. Narendra Modi is biggest OBC/MBC leader of India and he along with Nitish Kumar will attract a very big chunk of non-Yadav OBCs and MBCs. So, on paper NDA has a huge edge over INDI alliance in Bihar as far as Lok Sabha election is covered. It will be tough for NDA to repeat the 2019’s tally of 39 seats but they can still win 35 plus seats and if there is an undercurrent of Ram Mandir, then NDA can even win Mulsim domiated Kishanganj (with little indirect help of Owaisi). There is no doubt that BJP’s core supporters and many neutral Biharis are upset with Nitish Kumar coming back in NDA. But their support for Modi is much bigger than their hate of Nitish Kumar. We can’t vote for Rahul Gandhi just because we don’t like Nitish Kumar. As of now it seems that the game may be over for the INDI Allaince in Bihar unless something dramatric happens in next 3 months. Note - I have discussed the reasons of Nitish Kumar’s return into NDA in this answer.

Name: Achal
Question: Why has Nitish Kumar decided to return to the NDA fold after severing ties with the BJP in August 2022?
Answer: Nitish Kumar has a lifelong desire - to become PM or at least become PM candidate. This desire has dedicated his politics since 2010. One reason Nitish had left the NDA in 2022 was to become opposition’s PM candidate. Once it was clear that Congress would not even make his convenor of INDI Alliance, there was nothing left for Nitish in INDI Alliance. It is believed that Rahul Gandhi had promised him the role of convenor/head of opposition alliance and that is why it was Nitish Kumar who had worked hard to start the INDI Alliance. But Rahul Gandhi failed to fulfill his promise or the promise was false. So if Nitish had to be content with the post of CM, any day he would prefer to be with BJP. In 2017, when it became clear that there would be no united opposition alliance, Nitish dumped RJD & Congress and joined the NDA. As Modi’s election prospect of 2024 is very bright and opposition hope is dwindling, Nitish Kumar has switched side again. Nitish Kumar has always been very comfortable in running the Government with BJP. Its difficult to work with Lalu Yadav and his family. This time Lalu Yadav was trying to break JD(U) so that his son Tejashwi Yadav can become CM. Lalu was also pressurizing Nitish to give up the post of CM. Nitish Kumar who is also known as “Kursi Kumar” would not have left the post of CM of Bihar so easily. Many surveys were showing that NDA and INDI Allaince may each win 15 to 25 seats (or 20–20 seats) in Bihar in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. The Ram temple issue may have dented the INDI Alliance. At best JD(U) would have won 7–8 Lok Sabha seats as part of INDI alliance and now with NDA JD(U) can hope to win double digit Lok Sabha seats. I personally don’t like Nitish Kumar. His first term (2005–10) was one of the best era for Bihar, but subsequently Nitish Kumar’s train has got derailed & Bihar has suffered. Ideally, BJP should not have joined hands with Nitish Kumar. But politics has no moral ground and by definition, the main aim of a political party is to grab power. All parties are doing the same to remain in power. Nirish Kumar was, is and will remain the ultimate “Paltu Ram” of Indian politics.

Name: Achal
Question: Samajwadi party has given 11 seats to Congress in UP for 2024 Lok Sabha election. Do you think that SP-Congress-RLD alliance will be able to make an impact in UP?
Answer: Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav unilaterally announced an alliance with Congress Party in UP for 2024 Lok Sabha election. His party also gave the breakup of the alliance - SP (along with smaller parties like Apna Dal(K), Mahan Dal etc.) - 62 seats, Congress - 11 seats and RLD - 7 seats. But Congress later said that the seat sharing has not been finalized and the talks are still going. It seems that Congress was demanding 20 plus seats and SP was not ready to give more than 7 seats. Now SP has unilaterally announced 11 seats for Congress and it seems that the final number for Congress may be around 11 (or a couple of seats more than this). Irrespective of Nitish’s future move, Tejashwi Yadav may not become CM before 2025 assembly election and at worst they may end up in opposition. We don’t know what would happen in Bihar in 2024. There are two possibilities - 1) Nitish may go back to NDA or 2) Nitish may be using the opportunity & negotiations with BJP to keep Lalu Yadav in check while being in INDI Alliance.

Name: Achal
Question: How do you see the vandalization of English signboards in Bengaluru?
Answer: This is nothing but just politics by certain groups and we all know that they are backed by the ruling Congress party. Vandalism is always bad and the images of some activists / goons attacking English signboards in Bengaluru got its fair share of attention in social and traditional media. The police was just there for name’s sake and they didn’t enforce the rule of law by force. There is a rule to have Kannada written in signboards but it was not followed. BBMP recently gave a few weeks to business owners to have Kannada language on at-least 60% of the signboard. But some Kannada activists took law into their hand and started attacking English signboards. The law having Kannada on signboard in not new and it comes into limelight from time to time just for political reasons. Bengaluru is the capital city of Karnataka and Kannada is the official language of the state. Our 5 cr. Brothers and sisters speak the language as their native language. Kannada is a very old language and it must get the respect it deserves. I don think that Kannada doen’t get that much attention that it should get and many times its overshadowed by Hindi, English and Tamil. Even Kannada film industry is not as developed as Tamil and Telugu film industry. The KGF film franchises have managed to change this aspect but lot of things need to be done. Now Kannada has become a mandatory subject in all schools (CBSE, ICSE, or State Board). So, the younger generation (mainly from non-Kannada speaking background) will have a better understanding of the subject in the future. But this hooliganism of attacking shops and housing societies on the name of the signboard is not good. This one-off incident may not affect the city’s prospect in the long term but if such things are repeated, then it will certainly damage the city. Once, I had to cancel my flight to Germany when such vandalism happened the Kaveri Kaveri dispute and there was a curfew in certain parts of the city. Such protests are not very common in the city but if the frequency of such kind of protests and vandalism increases then it will be a problem for Bengaluru. I hope the Congress party would not fuel such vandalism. They may get some additional support in the city, but then every action will have its own reaction & Congress, being a national party, must refrain from such regional politics. And all businesses must follow the law of the land. The funny thing is that these activists don’t dare to protest in certain areas like Shivajinagar or Coxtown or KJ Halli. If they have guts, they must go to every part of the city where Kannada boards are missing. Let's see some of the interesting & funny reactions on social media (no offence to anyone)-

Name: Achal
Question: What roles do you think Shivraj Singh Chouhan could undertake in the Bharatiya Janata Party?
Answer: Shivraj Singh Chouhan is a leader who draws a lot of emotion and sympathy when he loses out the post of CM across India and mainly in MP. In 2018, when BJP narrowly lost election to Congress, Shivraj Singh Chouhan (Mama ji) got lot of love and attention from people. It seemed as a section of voters were expressing their sorrow for not voting for Mama ji. Fast forward to 2023, BJP has not made Shivraj Singh Chouhan CM again and he is drwing a lot of sympathy from everyone (from BJP voters to anti-BJP leftist liberals). Mama ji is yet but 65 years old and he has lot of politics left in him. At this age he has been CM of one of India’s largest state for 18 years. His political journey may move to Centre now. Even though Shivraj was from Adavani camp during the 2013 leadership contest, he has politically survived in Modi-Shah era. He will certainly move to Central politics next year. He is a versatile leader and can do wonders in central role. There are many options - he can succeed J P Nadda as BJP national President after Lok Sabha election, he can become Defence minister or a heavyweight agriculture minister. He is a prominent OBC leader of India and the most popular leader in Central India and BJP can’t ignore him. He will certainly get a big role in national politics.

Name: Achal
Question: DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran has said that “ Hindi Speaking people are cleaning roads and cleaning Toilets for us”. Why is DMK insulting Hindi speakers?
Answer: The level of bigotry that a section of Dravidian politics spews shames every other political outfit in India. Such attacks on Hindus and native Hindi speakers have increased a lot in recent months. A big section of Dravidian ideology has always given anti-Hindi and anti-Hindi statements. Now Dayanidhi Maran has insulted Biharis by saying that Biharis come to Tamil Nadu to clean toilets. This is an insult of Bihar and UP. The time has come when we Biharis need to teach such politicians/alliance a fitting lesson. Yes, many Biharis do work in Tamil Nadu but it doesn’t mean that politicians can insult us in such ways. Bihari labors play a critical role in many industrial belts of the state. The day all Bihari labors leave the state, many industrial units would face the labor shortage. It’s two way street - Bihar has labors and Tamil Nadu needs those labours. The time has come for people of Bihar to unite against INDI Alliance. Either the alliance force DMK leaders to apologize for their anti-Hindu and anti-Hindi statements or DMK should be expelled from the alliances. If such things are not done, INDI alliance would lose certainly loose the 2024 Lok Sabha election. There are many election issues but the pride of Bihar must be paramount importance for Biharis. Till the time DMK is in the INDI alliance, we must not give a single seat to INDI alliance in the state. And DMK is not alone and many Congress leaders from South India are giving similar statements. One day they talk about eradicating Hindus, the other day they insult Bihari DNA and the next day they say that Biharis are toilet cleaners. I have lived in South India for long and our South Indian brothers and sisters don’t think the same way as these leaders. DMK is under pressure due to its failure in handing the flood situation in state and that’s why they are going anti-Hindi speakers and anti-Hindu statements. The time has come to teach such politicians a fitting lesson.

Name: Achal
Question: Bajrang Punia left the Padma Shri award in front of PM Modi's residence in Delhi. Is this act justified?
Answer: There is no provision of returning Padma awards. The recipients of Padma awards are asked whether you would like to receive this award or not. Once they say Yes then only they receive these awards. As per Times of India “They only allow cancellation and annulment of the awards by the President, without specifying the grounds. The awardee continues to be in the register of Padma recipients maintained under directions of the President, until his/her award is annulled. The rules provide for cancellation of such annulment by the President”. The list[1] of people who have “returned” the Padma awards is very long. Bajrang Punia is a citizen of democratic country and he had all the democratic rights. He has rights to keep his Padam Shri aware anywhere. But if he is true to his cause, ideally he should have put the money received in Padma Shri and all the grants he has received from Central Government. But it’s his personal choice. Sakshi Malik and Bajrang Punia are now trying to dictate their wish on the country and federation. They are now demanding that the new wrestling federation President Sanjay Singh (who won a democratic election in the federation) should step down. They are not happy with Sanjay Singh because Sanjay Singh is a friend of former westing federation President Brijbhushan Singh. It’s like a few Indian cricket players demanding removal of BCCI President. Sakshi and Punia are good players but they can’t dictate the term on the federation. Bajrang Punia and Vignesh Phogat were given direct entry in recent Asian games without national trial and it denied other wrestlers to compete fairly. These both lost very badly in the games which can happen to any sportsperson. Delhi police has filed FIR and chargesheet against Brijbhushan Singh and now law will take its own course. Brijbhushan was removed as federation President and no one from his family contested the election. Is being friend of Brijbhushan a crime in India? These wrestlers refused to accept the finding of Mary Kom led committee. Mary Kom is the most respected sportsperson of India and they manhandled the greatest women athlete of our times PT Usha. You are good but these greats command way more respect than you. The timing of resurfacing of this issue is very interesting. Congress party was in backfoot in the issue of mimicry of VP (who happens to be a Jat). So they wanted an issue in which they can show BJP anti-Jat. Ao they are using Sakshi and Bajrang to show that BJP is anti-Jat. The main goal is 2024 Haryana Lok Sabha and assembly election.

Name: Achal
Question: Should Sonia Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge attend the inauguration of Ram Mandir?
Answer: Lets start with Sonia Gandhi. In my opinion she must attend the inauguration of Ram temple. It would be a tribute to her late husband Rajiv Gandhi. It was Rajiv Gandhi who ordered the opening of the locks on the Ramjanmabhoomi-Babri Masjid in Ayodhya removed. Till that time, a Hindu priest had been permitted to perform puja once a year for the idols installed there in 1949. After Rajiv Gandhi’s decision, all Hindus were given access to perform Pooja of Lord Ram. Even though that was a small step in 500 years struggle for the Ram temple, it proved to be very crucial. I will not go into the reasons of Rajiv Gandhi’s order but he passed that order. So, Sonia Gandhi must go to the inauguration of Ram Temple for the sake of her late husband. I don’t know the current religion of Sonia Gandhi. But Sonia Gandhi has been a wife of a Hindu and mother of two Hindus (as claimed by the Gandhi family). So, as a member of a Hindu family and mother of a “Jenau dhari” Brahmin, she should attend the historic day. Mallikarjun Kharge should also attend the ceremony as the President of India’s second largest political parties whose majority of voters are Hindus. Mallikarjun Kharge’s mother and sister was burned by the same force which had destroyed the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. And now, after centuries of struggle, we are going to reclaim one of the holiest place of Hindus. Yes, Hindus may not have treated the Dalits with dignity in past but now things are changing. Kharge himself a dalit is the president of Indian’s oldest political party and we had two Dalits PM. As one of the tallest Dalit leader of current times, Kharge should attend the ceremony on behalf of Congress voters and Dalits. But we don’t know what the leftist lobby of Congress would decide. Ideally, both should go to Ayodhya and be part of the historic moment.

Name: Achal
Question: Mamata Didi of TMC and CM of West Bengal has proposed Mallikarjun Kharge’s name for the PM post for the next elections. How do you feel about this proposal?

Name: Achal
Question: Who is the most successful captain in the history of world cricket?
Answer: It has to be MS Dhoni. He is the best captain in the world, cricket. His achievements are as - ODI world cup, T20 World Cup, ICC Champions trophy, no. 1 test team ranking (there was no test championship at that time). In franchise cricket- he has 5 IPL trophy (out of 16) and two T20 Champions League (out of 6). Can you find a captain who has won much trophies? Dhoni’s test record is not that great (27 wins out of 60 tests) but we must understand the time when Dhoni was captaining Indian test team. At that time, Indian pace attack was average, and you need gun fast bowlers to win in SENA countries. Doni’s test era coincided with the last phase of Indian batting greats (Sachin, Darvid, Laxman and Sehwag). With all these players in Indian team, India lost 4–0 in England and Australia. And once these players were gone, Dhoni held the Indian test team in the transition period. Any team would struggle with the loss of Sachin, Darvid, Laxman, and Sehwag. But he build a base in that transition period with which Virat conquered the world. Under Dhoni’s captaincy India nurtured the talent like Virat and Rohit. Rohit’s ODI record was below average till the 2013 Champions trophy but once he was promoted to open, he became a different player all together. It was Dhoni who gave all 4 tests to Viart during Virat’s first Australia tour despite failure in first two tests. He nurtured many players like Ashwin and Jadeja (world’s best test bowling pair for many years). Dhoni is the only captain in the Indian cricket history who nurtured another captain in Virat Kohli. Dhoni groomed him the day he felt that Virat has come on his own in test cricket he left test captaincy during 2015 Australian tour. And then for over a year he groomed Virat for white ball captaincy. For a generation of Indian players like Virat Dhoni would always remain their Captain. Dhoni is more a film director than a Captain. He decided about the role and then picks the player and give them freedom to perform the task. You will not find a more calm player than Dhoni in cricket,. His ability to nurture & rediscover talent is unparalleled. He will always remain the best cricket captain for me. Other great captains in my opinion are Allan Border, Imran Khan, Saurabh Ganguly, Clive Lloyd, Arjuna Ranatunga, Steve Wagh etc.

Name: Achal
Question: How would the Dominion of South Indian States work?
Answer: As per Birtannica, the Imperial Conference of 1926 described Great Britain and the dominions as “autonomous within the British Empire, equal in status, in no way subordinate one to another in any aspect of their domestic or external affairs, though united by a common allegiance to the Crown and freely associated as members of the British Commonwealth of Nations”. So in Indian context if it happens then the the dominion would be linked to India with the post of President. It would mean a fully autonomous state within India (equal to India and having rights for succession). But succession is not allowed in Indian constitution and Indian constitution makes Central Government very powerful compared to state Government. Till the time there is a strong India, such succession is unthinkable. Our South Indian brothers and sisters are as proud about India as any other Indian. And a tiny section of leftist liberals (irrespective of their residency) are always anti-India. Those dreaming about a separate or fully autonomous South India should first solve the Kaveri river water dispute and dispute between Andhra & Telangana. Even today a lot of Telugu speakers think that Chennai was a Telugu city and it was wrongly given to Tamil Nadu (Andhra Pardesh had claims on Chennai). And which political party would rule such state? As per today’s LoK Sabha numbers BJP is number one party in South India closely followed by Congress. And in case Congress would support such thinking then it would be wiped off from rest of India. Will DMK accept TDP, BRS, YSRCP as equals? Remember DMK dropped the demand of seperate county after seeing the patriotism of our Tamil brothers and sisters in 1962 India-China war. Such thinking is absurd and foolish.

Name: Achal
Question: Mohan Yadav has become the CM of MP. Do you think that BJP can get Yadav votes in UP & Bihar with this move?
Answer: BJP choice of Dr. Mohan Yadav as CM of MP has created a new buzz in Indian politics - Will Yadav community support BJP outside MP? Mohan Yadav is the only Yadav CM in today’s India. The larger Yadav community umbrella is very big in some of the North Indian states. Yadav community is the biggest caste in Bihar (as per the caste census) and one of the biggest communities in UP. Bith Bihar and UP have very strong Yadav parties in form of RJD and SP, respectively. BJP has been trying hard to have a foothold in the Yadav community but they have failed (more in assembly election). In Bihar, Yadavs are firmly with RJD and in Up they fully support SP. But over the years, BJP has become the second preference of Yadavs in some pockets of UP and Bihar. SP and RJD have been trying hard to brand BJP as anti-Yadav party. These parties along with Congress are also trying to brand BJP as anti-OBC on the caste census issue. But now BJP has given the post of MP CM to the Yadav community. Yadavs are in relatively small number in MP (around 4% to 5% of the population). Mohan Yadav may not politically influence Yadav community of UP and Bihar but his appointment is symbolic. BJP is giving signal to the Yadav community that BJP is not anti-Yadav. If The Yadav community votes for them in big numbers they would be be given appropriate representation. Also, these two Yadav parties are family party. In SP the top posts and the post of CM is reserved for Mulayam Singh Yadav family and in RJD all the top posts (including CM) is reserved for Lalu Yadav’s family. There are millions of educated and more able Yadav youths in Bihar but Lalu Yadav wants to make his 9th pass son the CM of Bihar. BJP wants to give signal that an ordinary Yadav politician can become CM only in BJP and not in SP & RJD. This may not results in votes now in Bihar and UP now but it may result in long term “goodwill” factor for BJP. And who knows this can turn into votes in future.

Name: Achal
Question: What factors might have contributed to the BJP's decision to choose Bhajanlal Sharma, a first-time MLA, as the Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
Answer: Many factors influenced BJP’s choice of selecting the CM face for Rajasthan - Image Source - India Today This is a new BJP not the Baniya Brahmin party of 1980s. BJP has embraced all caste and communities in its fold. BJP has given unprecedented representation to OBCs and SCs in union cabinet. Our last President was from SC community and the current President is a tribal woman. The PM is from an OBC community. In the Mandal 2 era, general casts have also emerged as a powerful vote bank in India. Brahmins & Baniyas have been a loyal BJP supporter for last few decades. Rajputs are also a formidable BJP supporter but in some key states they also vote for other parties. So, BJP is trying hard not to alienate general category also. So, they have given the post of Rajasthan CM to a Brahmin leader. Only time will tell whether this experiment would give desired results or not.

Name: Achal
Question: How do you see the BJP choice of CMs for MP, Rajasthan, and Chhattisgarh?
Answer: Politics is very ruthless, and there are only a few places at the top. So political parties have to be ruthless in bringing new leadership and generation change. BJP has brought new leadership forward in these three states. BJP had three tall leaders in these states. Shivraj Singh was CM for 18 years, Raman Singh for 15 years, and Vasundhara Raje was CM for 10 years. But we must remember that BJP lost all these three states last time under the leadership of these leaders. The loss in MP was narrow and the rebellion of Scindia helped JP to come back to power. Vasundhara Raje and Raman Singh remained largely politically inactive for four and half years. They almost gave to free field to Congress Government and other BJP leaders were more active. BJP has been trying to bring a generational change in leadership. In politics, succession plan and creating new leadership is very important to survive. Modi has tried to create new leadership in many states. Some experiments have worked like UP, Assam, Maharashtra and, to some extent, Haryana. These experiments have also failed in some states, like Jharkhand, Himachal Pradesh, Uttrakhand, etc. All these three leaders - Mohan Yadav, Vishnu Deo Sai and Bhajanlal Sharma are from RSS and AVBP background. Vishnu Deo Sai has been a Central minister and Mohan Yadav has been a senior Cabinet minister in MP. Bhajanlal Sharma has been an organizational person for life. Even if one or two of these three leaders become a strong leader, it would be very good experiment for BJP. Raman Singh will become speaker of Chhattisgarh (a retirement signal) and Shivaraj Singh may get either an important portfolio in Modi 3 Cabinet (if BJP wins the 2024 Lok Sabha election) or the post of BJP President. Vasundhara Raje may be accommodated on some symbolic post. Modi has been successful in implementing a generational change without much public outrage. And now these states need a new set of leadership and ideas. This also shows Modi’s grip on BJP. Image Source - The Print Let us look at the caste equation - Rajasthan CM - Brahmin Dy CMs - Rajput & SC Speaker - Baniya, Madhya Pradesh CM - OBC Dy CMs - Brahmin & SC Speaker - Rajput and Chhattisgarh CM - Tribal Dy CMs - Sahu (OBC) & Brahmin Speaker - Rajput. These days Rahul Gandhi has been talking about caste census and increasing the reservation. BJP has avoided commenting on the caste census but is trying hard to give representation to all caste groups. BJP hopes to get political mileage out of this decision. Only time will tell whether these decision will help BJP in the 2024 Lok Sabha election or not.

Name: Achal
Question: Is Vasundhara Rajay creating pressure on BJP leaders to make her Rajasthan’s new chief minister?
Answer: Yes, Vasundhara Raje did try to create some kind of pressure politics to become CM of Rajasthan for the third time. Vasundhara Raje has a history of internal rebelling against BJP high command and she has done it twice in past also. One famous incident was her rebellion when Rajanath Singh was BJP President. After that n a compromise was made between Rajnath Singh and Vasundhara Raje. This paved the way for Vasundhara Raje becoming the CM for second time. Some MLAs did try to go to a resort but they suddenly realized the mistake. Many MLAs did went to meet Vasundhara Raje but nothing materlaized. But this is a different BJP. Here you have to fall in line and Vasundhara Raje tried to show her strength but she had to give in. She had to propose the name of Bhajanlal Sharma in the legislative meeting and she also accompanied the CM elect to the Governor house. Unlike Advani and Vajpayee, Modi is a very powerful leader and he has the political strength to swing an election. So, Vasundhara Raje’s show of defiance failed. Vasundhara Raje is 70 years old and she can’t form a political party on her own. It will be difficult for her to join Congress. So she has limited option. And then the party high command might have promised a good political future for his son Dushyant Sing. Vasundhara Raje is at a age when she will have to think about her son’s future as well. Its quite natural that a powerful politician like Vasundhara Raje (who has no background in RSS or AVBP but has been in active politics since 1980s) will use all of their influence & power to become CM. This is politics and this is quite fare.

Name: Achal
Question: How do you see the Supreme Court’s verdict on abrogation of article 370 and changing the status of J&K state?
Answer: This may be perhaps one of the greatest moments in Indian political history. Bhartiya Jana Sangh/BJP has been opposing Article 370 since 1951 and finally they have achieved this. Leftist Liberals, some J&K politicians, opposition parties, some Muslim leaders, Pakistan etc. have been saying for long that Indian can’t abrogate Article 370. Some leaders have threatened that India would lose J&K and some had threatened that there would be no one to hold the Indian flag in Kashmir valley. But BJP has kept its promised and abrogated the Article 370. I welcome the verdict of the Supreme Court. As per the SC, the Article 370 was a temporary provision due to war conditions. And once J&K ruler signed the instrument of accession, there was no special rights for Kashmir. This verdict is very plain and simple. Jammu & Kashmir remains an integral party of India and every resident of J&K has the same rights as any Indian. Isn’t is surprising that till now we were told that Article 370 is permanent and it is the only tie between India and Kashmir? We kept appeasing a small set of the people in kashmir appeasing and the ordinary Kashmiri suffered. There was a genocide of Kashmiri Pandits in the valley and India remained silent. Pakistan kept raising the Kashmir issue on international forums and we were told that kashmir is a disputed territory. Indian state denied equal rights to Kashmiri women, SCs, STs, West pakistani refugees on the name of Article 370 and 35a. Article 370 was anti-women, anti-SCs and anti STs. There was no reservation of SCs and STs in J&K. Non Kashmiri Indians were not allowed to buy land in the state. All Kashmiri women who were marrying non-resident were denied the rights of being Kashmiri. Thousands of West Pakistani Refugees (WPRs) were denied the rights of residents despite living there for over decades. The condition of kashmir has impoved a lot after abrogation of article 370. There will be some terror attacks but the overall condition has improved. Now the Kashmir issue for India is settled with only two exceptions - Pakistani Occupied Kashmir (POK) and China controlled Aksai Chin (now Aksai Chin is part of the Union territory of Ladakh) . There would ne no talks about J&K with Pakistan and Pakistan can do whatever it wants. One nation, One Flag, One Constitution for India. Thanks Modi and BJP for fulfilling their promises. This was the promise of BJP/ Jan Sangh since the days of Shayma Prasad Mukharji. Many generations of leaders, including Vajpayee, Advani, Nana ji Deskhmukh, Murli Manohar Joshi etc. fought for this and their successor Modi has delivered the promise. And the decision has got the stamp of the Indian Supreme Court. Remember this speech of Vajpayee ji in Lok Sabha - Three goals - Ram temple, Article 370 and UCC. two goals achieved and one will be achieved in Modi’s possible third term.

Name: Achal
Question: Indians in Quora like to bash China but are very timid against the USA. Is it because they can fall back on the USA in their career move more than with China?

Name: Achal

Name: Achal
Question: How many of you believe that Amit Shah is the most popular leader among the masses from the BJP after Modi?
Answer: Amit Shah is the third most popular leader of BJP after Modi and Yogi Adityanath. Amit Shah rise in politics has specular. He was no nobody before 2013 in the national politics. Question: Was Sachin a lone warrior in the 90s?
Answer: No, Savhin was not a lone warrior in the 1990s for Indian cricket. This I am telling by my experience as kid who had started watching cricket since early 1990s. Sachin had played some important innings like half-century against Pakistan in 1992 WC but none of his top 20 knocks came before September 1994. Once Sachin is promoted to opener in September 1994, he started to dominate ODI cricket. 1996 was a dream year for Sachin when he scored 9 centuries in a single year (still a world record) and in 1998 he scored 1894 runs in an year (a world record till now). Sachin was the axis of Indian ODI team between 1995 to 1997. This was the period when Sachin wicket would almost mean victory for the opposition team. Ganguly and Dravid started to play cricket regularly after 1996 WC and in next two years, they had established themselves in ODI side and by this time Ajay Jadeja was also at his peak. So, from 1997–98, Ganguly and Dravid started to share burden of batting in ODI with Sachin. In 1999 WC, Dravid topped the scoring charts while Ganguly was third. Next was Ajay Jadeja at 11th and Sachin was 15th. By the time of 2003 WC when Sachin had excellent WC (his record was broken only in 2023 WC for highest runs in a single WC) but Ganguly, Dravid and Sehwag were sharing the burden of ODI batting. In test, Sachin was an important batter but the Indian team was not as dependent on him as in ODI. in 1990s, India used to loose almost every test overseas and Sachin was scoring some centuries and Dravid & Ganguly arrived in 1996. Sachin was a lone warrior in ODI cricket (which was the most watched form of cricket then) from 1994/95 to 1997 when people would switch TV after Sachin’s wicket and that coincided with 1996 WC. So, there is a lot of misconception that Sachin was lone warrior in whole decade on 1990s in ODIs. Sachin was then the best ODI batter in the world but Indian team also had some very good batters and bowlers. Kumble emerged as the highest wicket taker in 1996 WC (Roger Binni - the current BCCI President and Shami remains the other bowlers to top that chart). Sachin was great but cricket is a team sports and you can;t win many matches just because of just one player.
